name: nitrite de sodium
description_en: A curing agent (E250) that fixes the pink colour of cured meat and blocks botulism. During curing and cooking it forms nitrosamines; IARC rates ingested nitrite leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

name: nitrite de potassium
description_en: A curing agent (E249) that fixes the pink colour of cured meats and blocks botulism. It forms nitrosamines during curing and cooking; IARC rates ingested nitrite leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

name: nitrate de sodium
description_en: A curing salt (E251) that the body converts to nitrite, which can then form nitrosamines. IARC rates ingested nitrate under conditions leading to endogenous nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic. The confirmed Group 1 classification applies to processed meat as a food, not to the additive on its own.

name: nitrate de potassium
description_en: A curing salt (E252) used in charcuterie and cheese. In the body it converts to nitrite and forms nitrosamines: IARC classifies ingested nitrate under conditions leading to nitrosation as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic.

name: formaldehyde
description_en: A preservative and disinfectant classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, causally linked to nasopharyngeal cancer and leukaemia. Banned as a direct food additive and prohibited in EU cosmetics.

name: dmdm hydantoin
description_en: One of the most common formaldehyde-releasing preservatives in shampoos and lotions. The formaldehyde it emits is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen; EU rules restrict its level and require warning labelling.

name: quaternium-15
description_en: A formaldehyde-releasing preservative and one of the strongest emitters of the group. Formaldehyde is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen; quaternium-15 is now prohibited in EU cosmetics.

name: diazolidinyl urea
description_en: A cosmetic preservative that works by slowly releasing formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is a known contact allergen and its use is capped under EU cosmetics rules.

name: imidazolidinyl urea
description_en: A widely used cosmetic preservative that releases formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is a recognised contact allergen and is restricted under EU cosmetics regulation.

name: bronopol
description_en: A preservative (2-bromo-2-nitropropane-1,3-diol) that slowly releases formaldehyde, an IARC Group 1 carcinogen. It is also a frequent cause of contact allergy, and its use in EU cosmetics is restricted.

name: plomb
description_en: A heavy metal with no safe level of exposure according to the WHO. It is strongly neurotoxic — particularly damaging to children's brain development — and banned in EU cosmetics. Inorganic lead compounds are rated IARC Group 2A.

name: cadmium
description_en: A heavy metal that accumulates in the kidneys and bones over a lifetime. Cadmium and its compounds are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens, linked to lung cancer. It reaches food through polluted soil.

name: arsenic
description_en: A heavy metal contaminant found in water, rice and some seafood. Arsenic and inorganic arsenic compounds are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens, linked to skin, lung and bladder cancer.

name: mercure
description_en: A heavy metal that is strongly neurotoxic, especially for the developing brain. Banned in EU cosmetics and tightly capped in fish and seafood. It accumulates in the body and is never safe at any deliberate dose.

name: benzene
description_en: An industrial solvent and petroleum by-product. IARC Group 1 human carcinogen with an established causal link to leukaemia. It has no legitimate use in food or cosmetics and appears only as a contaminant.

name: aflatoxine
description_en: A natural mold toxin that forms on poorly stored grains, nuts and spices. Classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen — the confirmed level. Chronic exposure damages the liver and is a leading cause of liver cancer.

name: ppd
description_en: Para-phenylenediamine, the base of most permanent dark hair dyes. A strong skin sensitiser that can trigger severe allergic reactions; it is capped in the EU and illegal in "black henna" temporary tattoos.

name: coal tar
description_en: A by-product of coal processing, historically used in anti-dandruff and psoriasis treatments and in dyes. Coal tars are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; untreated preparations are restricted in EU cosmetics.

name: ptfe
description_en: PTFE includes perfluorinated compounds (PFAS), nearly indestructible chemicals; PFOA is a confirmed human carcinogen (IARC Group 1), PFOS possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B). Avoid exposure.

name: alcool ethylique
description_en: Ethanol in alcoholic beverages is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen. It is linked to cancers of the mouth, throat, oesophagus, liver, colon and breast, and no safe intake level has been established.

name: viande transformee
description_en: Meat preserved by salting, curing, smoking or nitrites (bacon, ham, sausages, deli meats). Classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen in 2015: regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk. Best kept occasional.

name: salami
description_en: A dry fermented and cured sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification: nitrite curing and fermentation generate compounds tied to colorectal cancer.

name: saucisson
description_en: A dry-cured sausage preserved with salt and nitrites. It falls under processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, with regular consumption linked to colorectal cancer.

name: chorizo
description_en: A cured, paprika-spiced sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification: the curing and smoking process generates compounds tied to colorectal cancer.

name: mortadelle
description_en: An emulsified, cured pork sausage. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification, with regular consumption linked to a higher colorectal cancer risk.

name: bacon
description_en: Salted, cured and smoked pork. It falls under processed meat, classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogen in 2015: regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk through nitroso-compounds formed during curing.

name: jambon
description_en: Cured or cooked pork leg. As a processed meat it falls under the IARC Group 1 classification (2015): salting and nitrite curing generate compounds that raise colorectal cancer risk with regular intake.

name: saucisse
description_en: Sausages, including hot dogs and merguez, are processed meats classified IARC Group 1 human carcinogens (2015). Regular intake raises colorectal cancer risk; they are also high in salt and saturated fat.

name: pastrami
description_en: Brined, smoked and spiced beef. It falls under processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and carries a heavy salt load. Regular intake is linked to colorectal cancer.

name: jerky
description_en: Salted and dried strips of beef. It counts as processed meat, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and is also very high in sodium. Best kept as an occasional snack.

name: nitrosamine
description_en: Compounds formed when nitrites react with proteins in cured meat or under high-heat cooking. Several nitrosamines, including NDMA, are rated IARC Group 2A and are a main reason processed meat is classified Group 1.

name: hydroquinone
description_en: A powerful skin-lightening agent. Banned in EU cosmetics except for limited professional nail products, because it causes irreversible skin discolouration (ochronosis) and carries genotoxicity concerns.

name: rouge 3
description_en: Erythrosine (E127), a petroleum-based cherry-red dye. The FDA revoked its authorisation in food and ingested drugs in January 2025 after it caused cancer in male rats, with reformulation required by 2027.

name: acide borique
description_en: Boric acid (E284), a preservative now allowed in the EU for caviar only. It is classified as toxic to reproduction under EU chemical law and accumulates in the body, which is why its use is so tightly limited.

name: tetraborate de sodium
description_en: Borax (E285), permitted in the EU for caviar only. It is classified as toxic to reproduction under EU chemical law and banned from general food use in most countries, including the US.

name: sulfate de cuivre
description_en: Copper sulfate (E519), used as a processing aid and firming agent. Copper is essential in trace amounts but toxic in excess, causing liver and kidney damage, so food use is tightly capped.

name: acrylamide
description_en: A compound that forms when starchy foods are fried, roasted or baked at high heat. IARC rates it Group 2A, probably carcinogenic, and EFSA confirmed it raises cancer risk across all age groups.

name: glyphosate
description_en: The world's most used herbicide, found as a residue in cereals and legumes. IARC classified it Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2015, though EFSA reached a different conclusion.

name: viande rouge
description_en: Rich in bioavailable iron, zinc and vitamin B12, which support blood and immune function. IARC classified red meat as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2015, based mainly on colorectal cancer - which is why it belongs in a balanced diet as a regular but moderate item rather than a daily one.

name: hijiki
description_en: A brown seaweed that accumulates inorganic arsenic, an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, at levels far above any other edible seaweed. The food agencies of the UK, Canada and Ireland do not merely advise moderation: they advise not eating it at all, and choosing another seaweed instead.

name: huile de palme
description_en: A cheap refined fat used across industrial food. High-temperature refining forms 3-MCPD and glycidyl esters — glycidol is rated IARC Group 2A, probably carcinogenic — and EFSA set very low tolerable intakes. Also a major driver of deforestation.

name: huile de colza
description_en: Rapeseed (canola) oil, favourable in fatty acid profile but industrially refined at high heat, which degrades its omega-3 content and forms process contaminants. Cold-pressed versions are a better choice.

name: huile de tournesol
description_en: Sunflower oil, usually refined and very high in omega-6 fats. It oxidises readily when heated, generating harmful compounds, and its regular use tilts the diet away from omega-3 balance.
aliases: huile de tournesol à haute teneur en acide oléique

name: huile de soja
description_en: The most widely used oil in industrial food, refined at high heat and dominated by omega-6 fats. It is often derived from GM crops outside the EU and contributes to an inflammatory fatty acid balance.

name: huile de mais
description_en: Corn oil, an industrially refined oil very high in omega-6 fatty acids. An unbalanced omega-6 to omega-3 ratio is associated with chronic inflammation when consumed regularly.

name: huile de coton
description_en: Cottonseed oil, extracted from a non-food crop that is heavily treated with pesticides. It is very high in omega-6 fats and requires intensive refining to remove natural toxins such as gossypol.

name: huile vegetale
description_en: An unspecified blend, most often refined palm or rapeseed. The label hides which fat is actually used, and heavy industrial refining is typical of ultra-processed food that whole ingredients never require.

name: hydrogenated
description_en: Oil hardened by adding hydrogen to extend shelf life. Partial hydrogenation creates trans fats, which are strongly linked to heart disease and are now restricted in the EU and banned in the US.

name: gras trans
description_en: Trans fatty acids raise bad cholesterol while lowering the good kind, directly increasing cardiovascular risk. The WHO has called for their global elimination and there is no safe level of intake.

name: graisse interesterifiee
description_en: Fat rearranged chemically or enzymatically to replace trans fats and mimic their texture. It avoids trans fats but remains a laboratory-restructured fat, and its long-term metabolic effects are still debated.

name: huile de coco modifiee
description_en: Coconut oil that has been hydrogenated, fractionated or interesterified to change its melting point. These industrial treatments alter the fat structure and mark a heavily engineered product.
aliases: huile de noix de coco modifiee
huile de noix de coco modifiée

name: amidon modifie
description_en: A generic label covering any starch altered chemically or physically to thicken and stabilise industrial food, without saying which one. EFSA considers modified starches safe with no numerical ADI needed, but they are refined carbohydrates with no nutrients and one of the clearest markers of ultra-processing.

name: phosphate de diamidon
description_en: Distarch phosphate (E1412), a cross-linked modified starch used to hold texture through heating and freezing. Safe by EFSA standards, but purely technical and typical of ultra-processed products.

name: phosphate de diamidon acetyle
description_en: Acetylated distarch phosphate (E1422), a doubly modified starch used in sauces, ready meals and desserts. It adds texture and shelf life but no nutritional value, and marks a highly industrial recipe.
aliases: fécule de pomme de terre modifiée
fecule de pomme de terre modifiee
fécule modifiée de pomme de terre

name: pepperoni
description_en: A cured, fermented pork and beef sausage preserved with nitrites. It is a processed meat, high in sodium and saturated fat, and regular intake is linked to colorectal cancer risk.

name: proteines hydrolysees
description_en: Proteins broken down with acid or enzymes, which releases free glutamate and acts as a hidden flavour enhancer. The process can also generate unwanted by-products such as chloropropanols.

name: caseinate
description_en: Milk protein extracted with alkali and isolated from the rest of the dairy matrix. It is a purely technical ingredient used to bind and emulsify, and marks an industrially assembled recipe.

name: isolat de proteines
description_en: Protein stripped from its original food by industrial extraction, leaving no fibre, fat or micronutrients. Useful for boosting protein figures on a label, but a marker of a reconstructed product.

name: proteine de pois
description_en: Protein isolated from yellow peas by industrial extraction. It is a useful plant protein, but stripped of the fibre and micronutrients of the whole pulse.

name: proteine de feve
description_en: Protein extracted from fava beans, used to boost protein content in plant-based products. Nutritionally useful, though an isolate rather than a whole food.

name: substances laitieres modifiees
description_en: A vague label covering dairy fractions altered or recombined industrially. It tells the consumer nothing about what is actually inside and signals a reconstituted rather than a real dairy product.

name: acesulfame
description_en: An artificial sweetener (E950) roughly 200 times sweeter than sugar, often blended with aspartame. Approved in the EU and US with an acceptable daily intake of 9–15 mg/kg, but it is a marker of ultra-processed formulation.

name: aspartame
description_en: An artificial sweetener (E951) in diet drinks and sugar-free products. IARC classified it Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic, in 2023, while WHO's JECFA kept the daily limit at 40 mg/kg. Best not consumed daily.

name: bha
description_en: Butylated hydroxyanisole (E320), a synthetic antioxidant in fats, snacks and cosmetics. Classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic to humans, and flagged by EFSA as a suspected endocrine disruptor.

name: tbhq
description_en: Tert-butylhydroquinone (E319), a petroleum-derived antioxidant preservative. Not classified as a carcinogen by IARC, but high-dose animal studies show immune effects, and EFSA advises against use for infants.

name: colorant
description_en: Additives used to give or reinforce the colour of a food. This wording does not say which colourings are present. Their safety depends on the specific substance used. The presence of colourings mainly indicates a processed product.

name: annatto
description_en: A yellow-orange colouring (E160b) extracted from achiote seeds, one of the few plant-based dyes still widely used in industry. Generally well tolerated, though it can trigger allergic reactions in a small number of people.

name: tartrazine
description_en: Yellow 5 (E102), a synthetic azo dye. EU law requires a warning that it may affect children's activity and attention; it can also trigger reactions in people sensitive to aspirin.

name: jaune 6
description_en: Sunset Yellow (E110), a synthetic azo dye. EU law requires a warning that it may affect children's activity and attention, and the FDA is phasing it out of US foods.

name: ponceau 4r
description_en: Cochineal Red A (E124), a synthetic azo dye subject to the EU warning label on children's activity and attention. It is banned from food in the United States, Norway and Finland.

name: rouge 40
description_en: Allura Red (E129), a petroleum-derived synthetic dye. EU law requires a warning label stating it may affect children's activity and attention, and the FDA is phasing it out of the US food supply.

name: orange b
description_en: A synthetic dye whose only remaining approved use in the US is colouring hot dog and sausage casings. It has never been authorised in the European Union.

name: azorubine
description_en: Carmoisine (E122), a synthetic red azo dye. EU law requires a label warning that it may affect activity and attention in children, and it is not authorised in the United States.

name: bleu 1
description_en: Brilliant Blue FCF (E133), a petroleum-derived synthetic dye. It is authorised in the EU and US, but the FDA is working to phase it out of the American food supply by the end of 2027.

name: caramel ammoniacal sulfite
description_en: Caramel colour made with ammonia and sulfites (E150c/E150d). The process forms 4-methylimidazole, classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. EU rules cap its use, and California requires warning labelling above set levels.

name: caramel ammoniacal
description_en: E150c is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with ammonia and contains 4-MEI, classified as possibly carcinogenic (IARC Group 2B). Health considerations include potential carcinogenic effects.

name: caramel sulfite caustique
description_en: E150b is an ultra-processed caramel coloring produced with sulfites and associated with controversial by-products. The health implications of these by-products are uncertain.

name: colorant caramel
description_en: E150 is an industrial caramel coloring usually made by chemical processes involving ammonia or sulfites, generating possibly carcinogenic 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B). Its consumption may carry cancer risk concerns.

name: carraghenane
description_en: A seaweed-derived thickener (E407) used in dairy, plant milks and processed meat. Food-grade carrageenan is authorised, but studies link it to gut inflammation and it is banned in EU infant formula.

name: carraghenane degrade
description_en: Degraded carrageenan, also called poligeenan, is the low-molecular-weight form and is classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. It has no authorised use as a food additive.

name: cmc
description_en: Carboxymethylcellulose (E466), a synthetic thickener made from cellulose. A controlled human trial found it altered the gut microbiome and intestinal lining, and it is a strong marker of ultra-processed food.

name: polysorbate 80
description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E433) widely used in ice cream, sauces and dressings. Animal and cell studies link polysorbate 80 to thinning of the protective gut mucus layer and low-grade inflammation.

name: polysorbate 20
description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E432) derived from sorbitol and ethylene oxide. Authorised at limited levels, but emulsifiers of this family have been linked in studies to disruption of the gut barrier.

name: polysorbate 40
description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E434) used to blend fats and water in industrial food. Permitted at capped levels; animal studies on polysorbates suggest effects on gut bacteria and inflammation.

name: polysorbate 60
description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E435) common in whipped toppings and baked goods. It is authorised but purely technical, and its family has been tied to gut microbiome changes in research.

name: polysorbate 65
description_en: A synthetic emulsifier (E436) used in ice cream and frozen desserts to control texture. Regulated at low levels, it is a clear marker of an industrially engineered product.

name: acide glutamique
description_en: Glutamic acid (E620), the free amino acid behind the savoury "umami" taste. It is used to intensify flavour in industrial foods and signals a product built on additives rather than real ingredients.

name: msg
description_en: Monosodium glutamate (E621), a flavour enhancer that makes processed food taste richer. Regulators consider it safe at normal intake, but it is a reliable marker of ultra-processed food and can encourage overeating.

name: silicate alumino-sodique
description_en: Sodium aluminosilicate (E554), used to stop powders clumping. It contributes to dietary aluminium, which accumulates in the body and is why EFSA set a weekly tolerable intake.

name: silicate alumino-potassique
description_en: Potassium aluminosilicate (E555), an anti-caking and glazing agent. Like other aluminium-based additives, it adds to total aluminium exposure, which EFSA considers should be kept low.

name: silicate alumino-calcique
description_en: Calcium aluminosilicate (E556), an anti-caking agent that contributes to overall aluminium intake. EFSA has flagged dietary aluminium as a concern for accumulation in the body over time.

name: ferrocyanure de sodium
description_en: An anti-caking agent (E535) added to table salt to keep it free-flowing. Despite the alarming name, the cyanide is locked in a stable complex and EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels.

name: phosphate aluminium sodium
description_en: E541 is an acidic aluminum salt used in baking powders to control gas release; it adds aluminum and sodium, increasing exposure risks if heavily consumed.
aliases: phosphate acide d'aluminium et de sodium
phosphate d'aluminium et de sodium acide

name: azodicarbonamide
description_en: A flour treatment agent (E927) used to bleach dough and speed up baking. Banned in the EU and Australia, still permitted in the US. During baking it breaks down into semicarbazide and urethane, both flagged for cancer concerns.

name: potassium bromate
description_en: A flour improver (E924) classified IARC Group 2B, possibly carcinogenic. Banned in the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil and China, but still permitted in US bread. Residues can remain in the finished loaf.

name: citrate de sodium
description_en: E331 is an acidity-regulating salt made industrially from citric acid and sodium hydroxide with no natural food form; it is a benign additive but indicates ultra-processing.

name: carbonate de calcium
description_en: E170 is a natural source of calcium, an essential mineral beneficial for the body and safe at usual doses.

name: vinaigre en poudre
description_en: Vinegar dried onto a starch carrier, typically maltodextrin, to flavour crisps and seasoning mixes. It is a technical powder built for industrial dosing, not a natural vinegar.

name: tapioca dextrin
description_en: A modified starch derived from cassava, used to coat, bulk and thicken. Like other dextrins, it is a refined carbohydrate that raises blood sugar quickly and adds no nutrients.

name: cire de carnauba
description_en: A plant wax from the leaves of the Brazilian carnauba palm, used to glaze sweets, chewing gum, coffee beans and coated tablets. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2012 and found no genotoxicity concern and sufficient margins of safety at authorised uses. It is practically not absorbed by the gut - the same conclusion reached for candelilla wax (E902).

name: extrait d'epices
description_en: Spice extract is obtained by industrial solvent extraction, differing significantly from whole spices. Its processing may reduce natural benefits and alter health effects.

name: concentre de fruits
description_en: Fruit or vegetable juice boiled down to concentrate its sugars. Manufacturers use it to sweeten products while keeping a natural-sounding label; the fibre is gone and the sugar behaves like added sugar.

name: fumee naturelle
description_en: Smoke flavouring produced by condensing wood smoke. It can carry polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which is why EFSA has re-evaluated smoke flavourings and the EU has restricted several of them.

name: argent
description_en: Silver (E174), used as a decorative coating on confectionery. EFSA could not conclude on its safety in 2016, and its 2025 follow-up confirmed that the data on nanoparticle content, silver-ion release and genotoxicity are still inadequate. Nearly a decade on, its safety as a food additive remains officially unresolved.

name: edta
description_en: A synthetic chelator (E385) that traps metal ions to stop fats going rancid and colours fading. Authorised at limited levels, it can also bind minerals the body needs and does not occur in nature.

name: acides gras
description_en: Fatty acids (E570) used as anti-foaming and glazing agents rather than as a food fat. They are refined industrial derivatives, typical of processed formulations.

name: glycine
description_en: An amino acid (E640) used as a mild sweetener and flavour modifier. The body makes its own supply, and it is safe at the small amounts used in food.
aliases: sel de sodium de la glycine

name: butane
description_en: Butane, isobutane and propane (E943/E944) used as propellants in aerosol food products such as cooking sprays and whipped cream. They are technical gases with no nutritional purpose.

name: charbon vegetal
description_en: Vegetable carbon (E153), a black colourant made by carbonising plant material. It is authorised in the EU but adds no nutritional value and can bind medicines and nutrients in the gut.

name: hydroxyde de sodium
description_en: Sodium hydroxide (E524), caustic soda, used to adjust pH and to peel or treat foods such as pretzels and olives. Corrosive in concentrated form; its presence indicates industrial processing.

name: hydroxyde de potassium
description_en: Potassium hydroxide (E525), a strongly alkaline processing aid used to adjust acidity and treat cocoa. It is neutralised in the final product but marks a chemically processed recipe.

name: hydroxyde de calcium
description_en: Calcium hydroxide (E526), or slaked lime, used to treat corn (nixtamalisation) and adjust acidity. Harmless in the finished food, but corrosive in raw form and a sign of industrial processing.

name: silicate de sodium
description_en: Sodium silicate (E550), a technical anti-caking and preservation aid. It is strongly alkaline in concentrated form and serves purely industrial purposes, with no nutritional role.

name: sulfate d'ammonium
description_en: An industrial salt used in flour treatment, fermentation, and acidity control. Health: No major specific harm is established at permitted levels. Excessive quantities may irritate the digestive system.

name: phosphate d'os
description_en: Bone phosphate (E542), a calcium phosphate obtained by degreasing and calcining animal bones, used in small amounts to keep powders free-flowing. It is of animal origin, so it does not suit vegetarian, vegan, halal or kosher diets unless specifically certified, and it adds to total phosphate intake, which EFSA already considers high in European diets. Its use in food today is marginal.

name: parabene
description_en: A family of preservatives with weak hormone-like activity in laboratory tests. The EU banned five of them from cosmetics in 2014 for lack of safety data (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben) and capped propyl- and butylparaben at 0.14%, with an additional ban on the nappy area of children under three. The 2004 study that detected parabens in breast tissue established no causal link; the real issue is cumulative exposure across food, cosmetics and medicines.

name: phtalate
description_en: Plasticisers that soften plastics and fix fragrances. Several are classified as toxic to reproduction and act as endocrine disruptors; the most harmful are banned or authorisation-restricted in the EU.

name: cyclosiloxane
description_en: Cyclic silicones (cyclomethicone, D4, D5, D6) used for silky texture in hair and skin products. They are persistent in the environment and are progressively being restricted in EU cosmetics.

name: triclosan
description_en: An antibacterial agent in some toothpastes, soaps and deodorants. The FDA banned it from consumer hand soaps in 2016; it is capped in the EU over hormonal effects and its contribution to antibiotic resistance.

name: phenoxyethanol
description_en: A widely used preservative, permitted in the EU up to 1% in cosmetics. It is generally well tolerated, though France's health agency advised against using it on the nappy area of children under three.

name: oxybenzone
description_en: A chemical UV filter absorbed through the skin and repeatedly flagged for hormonal activity. Its permitted concentration has been reduced in the EU, and it is banned in Hawaii and Palau for coral reef damage.

name: octinoxate
description_en: A chemical UV filter (with homosalate and octisalate) that penetrates the skin and is detectable in blood. EU scientific committees have cut the permitted levels over endocrine-disruption concerns, and some regions restrict it to protect coral reefs.

name: aluminum chlorohydrate
description_en: The active salt in antiperspirants, which plugs sweat ducts to block perspiration. No link to breast cancer has been established, but it is absorbed in small amounts and adds to total aluminium exposure.

name: paraffinum liquidum
description_en: Liquid petroleum oil used as an emollient in cosmetics. Untreated and mildly treated mineral oils are IARC Group 1 human carcinogens; pharmaceutical-grade refining lowers the risk but MOAH residues remain a concern.

name: sirop de ble
description_en: A syrup made by breaking down wheat starch into sugars. It is marketed as a natural sweetener but behaves like any glucose syrup, with a high glycemic impact and no nutrients.

name: amidon
description_en: Starch extracted from grains or tubers, used to thicken and bulk out food. It is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and none of the fibre or nutrients of the original grain.

name: bicarbonate d ammonium
description_en: E503 is an industrial raising agent releasing carbon dioxide and ammonia during baking, common in dry biscuits and crackers. Poorly baked or heavily dosed products may retain ammonia odor and cause irritation, but normal use is not a major health risk.

name: sucre
description_en: Refined sucrose, stripped of every nutrient. It is absorbed rapidly, driving blood-sugar spikes and insulin resistance, and regular intake contributes to obesity, type 2 diabetes and chronic inflammation.

name: sucre de canne
description_en: Cane sugar, including raw, brown and demerara forms. It keeps a trace of molasses and minerals, but it is still around 95% sucrose and affects blood sugar much like white sugar.

name: sucre inverti
description_en: Sugar split into glucose and fructose to boost sweetness and keep products moist. Metabolically it behaves like table sugar, with the same effect on blood sugar and weight.

name: sucres
description_en: A catch-all label covering the added refined sugars in a product. They deliver energy with no vitamins, minerals or fibre, and regular consumption is tied to metabolic disease.

name: sirop de glucose-fructose
description_en: High-fructose corn syrup, a cheap industrial sweetener. Its fructose load is processed almost entirely by the liver and is linked to non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and metabolic syndrome.
aliases: sirop de maïs à haute teneur en fructose

name: sirop de glucose
description_en: A syrup produced by industrial hydrolysis of corn or wheat starch. It has a very high glycemic index, causes sharp blood-sugar spikes and brings no nutrients — a hallmark of ultra-processed food.

name: glucose
description_en: Added glucose in isolated form, absorbed almost instantly. It raises blood sugar faster than table sugar and carries no nutritional value beyond calories.

name: sirop de mais
description_en: Corn syrup is an industrial syrup made from often-GMO corn linked to obesity, fatty liver disease, and metabolic syndrome.

name: gelatine
description_en: Collagen extracted from animal skin and bone by acid or alkali treatment (E441). It is a safe, protein-based gelling agent, though of animal origin and low in nutritional value. Not suitable for vegetarians, or for halal and kosher diets unless certified.

name: sirop d'agave
description_en: Marketed as natural but industrially ultra-refined. Made of 70-90% isolated fructose that overloads the liver and promotes non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Consume in moderation.

name: sirop de riz
description_en: Rice syrup, often sold as a healthier sweetener. It is almost pure glucose with a very high glycemic index, and rice-based products can carry inorganic arsenic residues.

name: maltodextrine
description_en: An ultra-processed carbohydrate made by industrial hydrolysis of starch, often from corn. Its glycemic index reaches around 110, higher than table sugar, and studies link it to disrupted gut bacteria.

name: dextrose
description_en: Industrially refined pure glucose, usually from corn starch. Absorbed very rapidly, it causes sharp blood-sugar and insulin spikes with no nutritional benefit.

name: dextrine
description_en: A partially broken-down starch used as a thickener, binder and bulking agent. It is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and no nutrients.

name: fructose
description_en: Isolated fructose, very different from the fructose inside whole fruit, which comes with fibre and nutrients. It is metabolised by the liver and, in isolated form, promotes fat accumulation there.

name: jus de raisin concentre
description_en: Concentrated grape juice used to sweeten products without declaring added sugar. It is rich in fructose and behaves metabolically much like a syrup.

name: jus de pommes concentre
description_en: Concentrated apple juice, one of the most common "natural" sweeteners in industrial food. Nutritionally it is close to added sugar, with the fibre and most vitamins removed.

name: jus concentre
description_en: Juice boiled down to concentrate its sugars, then used to sweeten products while keeping a natural-sounding label. The fibre is gone and the sugar behaves like added sugar.

name: huile de pepin de raisin
description_en: Grapeseed oil, extracted from winemaking residue and usually solvent-refined. It is very high in omega-6 fats, which tilts the diet away from omega-3 balance when used regularly.

name: arome naturel
description_en: Despite the name, these are extracted and concentrated in industrial processes, often using solvents. The precise composition is a trade secret, and their presence signals a product engineered for taste rather than made from whole ingredients.

name: arome artificiel
description_en: Entirely synthetic molecules, usually petrochemical-derived, built to imitate natural tastes. Their exact composition is not disclosed on the label, and they are one of the clearest markers of ultra-processed food.

name: arome bio
description_en: Flavouring made from certified organic raw materials, which limits solvents and synthetic inputs. Still a concentrated industrial extract, but a step above conventional natural flavouring.

name: emulsifiant
description_en: Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids (E471), used to blend fat and water. Widely permitted, but they can contain traces of trans fats depending on the source oil, and they mark an industrial recipe.

name: lecithine de soja
description_en: A natural emulsifier extracted from soybeans or sunflower seeds, used to blend fat and water. It is well tolerated and one of the most benign emulsifiers, though soy versions are often solvent-extracted and may be GM.

name: pgpr
description_en: Polyglycerol polyricinoleate (E476), a synthetic emulsifier from castor oil used to cut cocoa butter costs in chocolate. Authorised in the EU, it signals a cheaper, more industrial formulation.

name: poudre a lever
description_en: Baking powder, a blend of a carbonate and an acid salt that makes dough rise. It is harmless in itself, though some formulations use aluminium-based acids that add to total aluminium intake.

name: gomme xanthane
description_en: E415 is an additive that may disrupt digestion in sensitive people. It can cause digestive issues for some individuals.

name: gomme guar
description_en: E412 is an industrial gelling agent that may cause bloating and digestive discomfort. It is used to thicken and stabilize foods.

name: gomme arabique
description_en: Acacia gum acts as a prebiotic fiber that nourishes beneficial gut bacteria.

name: gomme de caroube
description_en: Industrial thickener extracted from carob. May cause digestive issues (bloating, gas) and allergies in infants. Used in processed products.

name: gomme konjac
description_en: E425 is an additive that carries a risk of intestinal blockage. Care should be taken when consuming products containing it.

name: gomme tara
description_en: Industrial thickener with little long-term research. May cause digestive issues (bloating, gas). Its presence in a product indicates industrial processing.

name: gomme gellane
description_en: Industrial gelling agent produced by bacterial fermentation in a bioreactor. Digestive effects at high doses (bloating). A marker of ultra-processed food.

name: alginate
description_en: Gelling agent extracted from brown seaweed then converted to its sodium salt. Considered safe by EFSA (2017), but typical of industrial desserts, sauces and cheeses. Use in moderation.

name: alginate de potassium
description_en: Potassium salt of alginic acid from brown seaweed. Thickener deemed safe by EFSA, but its presence signals industrial manufacturing. Use in moderation.

name: alginate d'ammonium
description_en: A seaweed-derived thickener (E403) used to stabilise texture. It passes through the gut undigested and is considered safe at food levels.

name: alginate de calcium
description_en: Calcium salt of alginic acid, used for "spherified" textures and reconstituted foods (stuffed olives, reformed fruit). No identified risk, but typical of rebuilt foods. Use in moderation.

name: acide citrique
description_en: The acid that gives citrus fruit its sharpness - though the E330 on a label is produced industrially by fermenting sugar with Aspergillus niger, not extracted from lemons. It is one of the most benign additives there is, used to adjust acidity and protect colour. Its only real drawback is that it erodes tooth enamel in acidic drinks.

name: diphosphate
description_en: Diphosphates (E450) used as raising agents and to retain water in meat and seafood. They add to total phosphate intake, which EFSA capped in 2019 over cardiovascular and kidney concerns.

name: tripolyphosphate
description_en: A phosphate (E451) used to make meat and seafood hold water, increasing their weight. It is permitted but contributes to a phosphate load that EFSA considers already high in European diets.

name: polyphosphate
description_en: Polyphosphates (E452) used to bind water, emulsify and stabilise processed meat and cheese. They count toward EFSA's combined phosphate limit and are a clear marker of industrial processing.

name: phosphate de sodium
description_en: An added phosphate (E339) used to bind water and hold texture. Added phosphates are absorbed far more readily than natural ones, and EFSA has flagged high total intake as a concern for kidney and heart health.

name: phosphate de potassium
description_en: A phosphate salt (E340) used as a buffer and stabiliser. EFSA set a combined limit for all phosphate additives; people with reduced kidney function should keep added phosphates low.

name: phosphate de calcium
description_en: A phosphate salt (E341) used as an anti-caking agent and firming agent, and to fortify foods with calcium. It falls under EFSA's combined phosphate limit, which many diets already approach.

name: chlorure de potassium
description_en: A refined mineral salt used to replace sodium, control flavor, or support texture. Health: Excess potassium can cause dangerous heart-rhythm problems in people with kidney disease or certain medications. Normal consumers usually tolerate food amounts.

name: acide lactique
description_en: An acidity regulator (E270) produced by fermentation, the same acid found in yoghurt and sourdough. It is one of the safest additives, though industrial versions are made in fermenters, not from milk.

name: acide malique
description_en: E296 is an industrially synthesized compound rarely extracted from fruit. Its occasional use reflects its synthetic origin in food processing.

name: egcg
description_en: The main catechin in green tea, a well-studied antioxidant. Drunk as an infusion it raises no concern. As a concentrated extract it is a different matter: EFSA found in 2018 that 800 mg of EGCG per day or more from supplements raises liver enzymes, and the EU now requires warning labelling on green tea extracts. Read it as a good sign in tea, a caution in a supplement.

name: spiruline
description_en: A cyanobacterium dried into powder, dense in plant protein, iron and antioxidants. One caveat matters: the B12 it contains is pseudo-B12, inactive in humans, so it cannot be counted as a B12 source on a plant-based diet. Sourcing also matters, since poorly controlled production can carry microcystin contamination.

name: bouillon
description_en: Stock used as a flavour base. Homemade versions are nutritious, but industrial bouillon is usually dominated by salt, flavour enhancers and fat, with very little real meat or vegetable.

name: modified whey
description_en: Whey that has been chemically or enzymatically altered for texture and shelf life. It is far removed from the original dairy ingredient and is characteristic of ultra-processed formulation.

name: defatted soy flour
description_en: Soy flour with the oil removed by industrial solvent extraction, then used as a cheap protein filler. It is a highly processed commodity ingredient with little resemblance to whole soy.

name: imitation mozzarella
description_en: A cheese substitute built from vegetable oil, starch and milk proteins rather than curdled milk. It is engineered for melt and cost, and delivers none of the qualities of real cheese.

name: fromage allege
description_en: Reduced-fat cheese. Lower in calories, but manufacturers often compensate with added salt, starch or stabilisers, and the texture depends on more processing than full-fat cheese.

name: fromage fondu
description_en: Processed cheese made by melting cheese scraps with emulsifying salts, usually phosphates. It is high in sodium and phosphate additives and bears little resemblance to traditionally made cheese.

name: sodium benzoate
description_en: A preservative (E211) used in acidic drinks and sauces. Combined with vitamin C, and helped by heat or light, it can form traces of benzene — a reason to avoid drinks that list both.

name: benzoate de potassium
description_en: A preservative (E212) closely related to sodium benzoate. It can form traces of benzene when a product also contains vitamin C, and may trigger hives or asthma in sensitive people.

name: citrate de potassium
description_en: Industrially synthesized salt (citric acid + potassium hydroxide reaction). No natural form in food. A marker of ultra-processing. Laxative effect in excess.

name: stevia
description_en: Steviol glycosides (E960) extracted from stevia leaves — plant-derived but heavily refined. Approved with a daily limit of 4 mg/kg, they add no calories, though the aftertaste means they are often blended with other sweeteners.

name: bht
description_en: Butylated hydroxytoluene (E321), a synthetic antioxidant in fats, cereals and cosmetics. EFSA re-evaluated it as safe within a low daily limit; IARC does not classify it as carcinogenic.

name: dioxyde de soufre
description_en: A preservative and antioxidant (E220) common in wine, dried fruit and processed potato. It must be declared as an allergen in the EU above 10 mg/kg because it can trigger asthma attacks in sensitive people.

name: sulfite de sodium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E221) that keeps foods pale and stops spoilage. It is an EU-declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg and can provoke breathing problems in people with asthma.

name: bisulfite de sodium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E222) used to prevent browning and microbial growth. Like all sulfites it must be labelled above 10 mg/kg and can trigger reactions in sulfite-sensitive individuals.

name: metabisulfite de sodium
description_en: One of the most widely used sulfites (E223), found in wine, dried fruit and seafood. It destroys some thiamine (vitamin B1) and is a declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg in the EU.

name: metabisulfite de potassium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E224) common in winemaking and dried fruit. It must be declared as an allergen above 10 mg/kg and can cause asthma symptoms in sensitive people.

name: sulfite de potassium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E225) used to stop oxidation and spoilage. Safe for most people, but an EU-declarable allergen that can trigger breathing difficulties in asthmatics.

name: sulfite de calcium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E226) used mainly in processed vegetables and drinks. It is a declarable allergen above 10 mg/kg and best limited by anyone sensitive to sulfites.

name: bisulfite de calcium
description_en: A sulfite preservative and firming agent (E227). It carries the same allergen labelling requirement as other sulfites and can provoke asthma symptoms in sensitive individuals.

name: bisulfite de potassium
description_en: A sulfite preservative (E228) used in wine and processed fruit. Like the whole sulfite family, it must be declared above 10 mg/kg and can trigger reactions in sulfite-sensitive people.

name: sorbate de potassium
description_en: One of the most common mould inhibitors (E202), well tolerated and among the gentler preservatives. Some laboratory work suggests it may react with vitamin C, though food-level effects are not established.

name: propionate de calcium
description_en: A mould inhibitor (E282) used mainly in industrial bread. It is considered safe by EFSA and occurs naturally in some cheeses, though its presence signals bread built for long shelf life.

name: erythorbate de sodium
description_en: An antioxidant (E316) that is a mirror-image form of vitamin C, used to keep cured meat pink and fats fresh. It is safe, but it has no vitamin activity and appears mostly in processed meat.

name: bleu 2
description_en: Indigotine (E132), a synthetic blue dye made from petroleum. Authorised in the EU and US, it is among the six certified dyes the FDA is pushing manufacturers to remove.

name: jaune de quinoléine
description_en: Quinoline Yellow (E104), a synthetic dye carrying the mandatory EU warning about effects on children's activity and attention. It is not authorised as a food colour in the United States.

name: vert 3
description_en: Fast Green FCF (E143), a synthetic dye that is not authorised as a food colour in the European Union. It remains permitted in the US, where the FDA is working to phase it out.

name: dioxyde de titane
description_en: A white colouring (E171) used in sweets, sauces and supplements. The EU banned it as a food additive in August 2022 after EFSA concluded that a concern for genotoxicity could not be ruled out and that no safe daily intake could be set. It remains permitted in the United States and in cosmetics.

name: cochenille
description_en: Carmine (E120), a red colour made from crushed cochineal insects. It is natural rather than synthetic, but it is a recognised allergen that has caused severe reactions, and it is not vegetarian.

name: silice
description_en: Silicon dioxide (E551), an anti-caking agent in powders and dried mixes. EFSA could not confirm the safety of its nanoparticle fraction in its re-evaluation and called for stricter specifications.

name: saccharine
description_en: One of the oldest artificial sweeteners (E954). Once suspected of causing bladder cancer in rats, it was later cleared for humans and delisted as a carcinogen, but remains a purely synthetic additive.

name: sucralose
description_en: A chlorinated artificial sweetener (E955) about 600 times sweeter than sugar. Approved by EFSA and the FDA, but studies suggest it may disturb gut bacteria, and it can form harmful compounds when heated in baking.

name: cyclamate
description_en: An artificial sweetener (E952) still permitted in the EU but banned in the US since 1969 after bladder tumours appeared in rats. It has one of the lowest acceptable daily intakes of any sweetener.

name: extrait de levure
description_en: Yeast broken down to release its natural glutamate, giving a savoury boost without an “MSG” label. It is safe, but it plays the same role as a flavour enhancer while sounding more natural.

name: acide guanylique
description_en: E626, guanylic acid, is an umami flavor enhancer that boosts MSG effects and is not advised for people with gout due to purines.

name: guanylate disodique
description_en: E627, disodium guanylate, is an umami enhancer in instant soups that multiplies MSG effects and is not advised for gout sufferers.

name: guanylate dipotassique
description_en: Dipotassium guanylate (E628) is a potassium variant umami enhancer not advised for people with gout.

name: guanylate de calcium
description_en: Calcium guanylate (E629) is a ribonucleotide flavor enhancer that boosts savory taste; not advised for people with gout due to purines.

name: acide inosinique
description_en: E630, inosinic acid, is an umami enhancer from bacterial fermentation that boosts MSG taste and is not advised for people with gout.

name: inosinate disodique
description_en: Disodium inosinate, an umami enhancer in chips and broths, often combined with MSG. Sometimes derived from animal sources (fish, pork) — a point of caution for vegetarians. Not advised for gout.

name: inosinate dipotassique
description_en: Dipotassium inosinate (E632) is a potassium-based ribonucleotide flavor enhancer used in reduced-sodium recipes; not advised for people with gout.

name: inosinate de calcium
description_en: E633, calcium inosinate, is a rare umami enhancer from ribonucleotides and is not advised for people with gout.

name: ribonucléotides calciques
description_en: E634, calcium ribonucleotides, is a blend of calcium salts of inosinic and guanylic acids used as an umami enhancer and not advised for gout.

name: ribonucleotides
description_en: Disodium ribonucleotides (E635) are a blend of E627 and E631 that enhance flavor and are often combined with MSG.

name: anthocyanes
description_en: Purple-red pigments (E163) extracted from grape skins, berries or red cabbage. They are plant-derived and carry antioxidant activity, but the food-grade version is a concentrated industrial extract.

name: chlorophylle
description_en: Green plant pigments (E140/E141) used as colouring. The natural form is benign; the copper-stabilised version used for brighter colour adds a small amount of copper to the diet.

name: d-alpha tocopherol
description_en: The natural RRR form of vitamin E, the one with the highest vitamin activity in the body. It protects cells and dietary fats from oxidation. EFSA re-evaluated the tocopherol family (E306-E309) in 2015 and found no safety concern at the levels used in food.

name: alpha-tocopherol
description_en: Vitamin E, a natural antioxidant found in plants and foods (vegetable oils, nuts, seeds).

name: gamma-tocopherol
description_en: E308 is a natural form of vitamin E (gamma-tocopherol) from vegetable oils that acts as an antioxidant.

name: delta-tocopherol
description_en: E309 is a natural form of vitamin E (delta-tocopherol) from vegetable oils that acts as an antioxidant.

name: acide succinique
description_en: E363 is an industrial acidifier with limited long-term research available. Its health effects are not fully understood, so use is occasional.

name: citrate triammonique
description_en: E380 is an industrial ammonium salt with limited toxicological data available. Its safety profile is not well established, so consumption should be occasional.

name: tanin ferrique
description_en: Iron tannate (E181), a colouring used on olives and some coatings. It is permitted at low levels but has little modern use and adds no nutritional value.

name: or
description_en: Gold leaf (E175) used to decorate confectionery and drinks. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2016 and concluded that, given the very low solubility of elemental gold, systemic absorption and systemic effects are not expected. It passes through the body unchanged and adds nothing nutritionally - purely decorative.

name: sulfate de magnesium
description_en: E518 is an industrial laxative at high doses that can disrupt electrolyte balance. Excessive intake may cause health issues.

name: stearate de magnesium
description_en: E572 is an industrial lubricating agent that may reduce nutrient absorption. Its use should be occasional to minimize potential effects.

name: glucono-delta-lactone
description_en: A glucose-derived compound that slowly releases gluconic acid, helping set tofu, cure foods, and control acidity. Health: Large amounts may cause bloating, gas, or digestive discomfort.

name: thon
description_en: A nutritious source of protein and omega-3, but a large predator that accumulates methylmercury. Health agencies advise limiting intake, particularly for pregnant women and young children.

name: tilapia
description_en: A widely farmed white fish, affordable and lean but low in omega-3 and relatively high in omega-6. Farming conditions vary considerably, so sourcing matters.

name: saumon d'elevage
description_en: Farmed salmon is raised intensively with industrial feed, antibiotics, synthetic colorants, and possible contaminants like PCBs and dioxins; wild salmon is preferable.

name: tarama
description_en: A spread made from salted fish roe. Traditional versions are simple, but industrial tarama is dominated by oil, salt and colouring, with a modest proportion of actual roe.

name: tobiko
description_en: Flying fish roe used in sushi. It provides protein and omega-3, but it is very high in sodium and commercial versions are usually dyed and preserved.

name: melasse de malt
description_en: A natural syrup made by concentrating sprouted barley malt.

name: sucre de canne complet
description_en: Unrefined cane sugar (rapadura, panela, muscovado, jaggery) keeps the molasses and with it iron, potassium and polyphenols that white sugar has lost. It is nonetheless still 85 to 95% sucrose and behaves in the body much like table sugar. Better, not harmless.

name: carbonate de sodium
description_en: Sodium carbonate (E500), an acidity regulator and raising agent used in noodles, baked goods and cocoa. It is neutralised in the finished food but contributes sodium and marks industrial processing.

name: soja
description_en: Soy in unspecified form, from whole beans to industrial isolates. Whole soy is nutritious, but most soy in processed food is heavily refined and frequently GM outside the EU.

name: proteine de ble
description_en: Wheat gluten isolated by washing the starch out of the flour, then dried. It is protein-rich but low in lysine, and is used mainly to give industrial breads and meat substitutes their elasticity. Unsuitable in coeliac disease or gluten sensitivity.

name: proteine de soja
description_en: Soy protein isolated through industrial processing, often with hexane solvent. It is frequently GM-derived outside the EU and is used to bulk up protein content in reconstituted foods.

name: lait en poudre
description_en: Milk dried at high temperature for shelf life. It keeps most nutrients, though heat processing can oxidise some cholesterol and degrade certain vitamins compared with fresh milk.

name: farine de ble enrichie
description_en: White flour with a few vitamins and iron added back after refining stripped them out. The fortification helps, but the fibre and most micronutrients of the whole grain are gone for good.

name: pain blanc
description_en: Bread made from refined flour, with the bran and germ removed. It raises blood sugar quickly and delivers little fibre; wholemeal or sourdough versions are substantially better.

name: cyanocobalamine
description_en: A stable added form of vitamin B12, widely used in fortified foods and supplements and important for anyone eating little animal produce. Safe at normal intake; it marks a fortified rather than naturally rich product.

name: niacinamide
description_en: Vitamin B3 in its added form, used to fortify flours, cereals and drinks. The vitamin itself is beneficial and well tolerated; its presence mainly signals a refined product whose nutrients were added back after processing.

name: pantothenate de calcium
description_en: Vitamin B5 in its added form, used to enrich foods, drinks and supplements. Harmless and genuinely useful, but it usually appears in products that lost their natural nutrients during refining.

name: pyridoxine chlorhydrate
description_en: Vitamin B6 in its added form, common in fortified foods and supplements. It is effective and safe at normal levels; very high long-term supplement doses are the only real concern.

name: inositol
description_en: A sugar-like compound found naturally in fruits, beans and grains, and also produced by the body. Added to energy drinks and supplements, it is well tolerated, but the added form is more marketing than nutritional need.

name: cheddar deshydrate
description_en: Cheese powder used to coat crisps and season mixes. It is very high in sodium and often blended with flavour enhancers and anti-caking agents rather than being simply dried cheese.

name: fragrance
description_en: A single word hiding a mixture that can contain dozens of undisclosed compounds. EU law requires 26 known fragrance allergens to be named separately, which is why perfumed products are a leading cause of contact allergy.

name: peg-
description_en: PEG- are ethoxylated ingredients that may contain traces of 1,4-dioxane, a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B). Their quality depends on purification; limit use.

name: inuline
description_en: A prebiotic fibre from chicory root or agave that feeds beneficial gut bacteria. It is genuinely useful, but it is also one of the most fermentable fibres there is: added to industrial products to boost the fibre figure on the label, it commonly causes bloating and gas, and it is poorly tolerated in irritable bowel syndrome.

name: eau
description_en: Water hydrates the body without calories or additives, supporting all bodily functions.

name: sel
description_en: A mineral essential to the body's proper functioning (water balance, nerve transmission), but often present in excess in snacks and processed foods. High sodium intake is linked to high blood pressure. Use in moderation.

name: ble
description_en: Whole wheat - the intact grain with its bran and germ - supplies fibre, B vitamins, magnesium and plant protein. Refining strips most of that away, so the wholemeal version is a different food nutritionally from white flour.

name: avoine
description_en: Beta-glucan in oats helps lower cholesterol and provides slow-releasing energy to keep you full longer.

name: riz complet
description_en: Brown rice keeps its bran and germ, and with them fibre, B vitamins, magnesium and manganese that support digestion and energy production. White rice is the same grain with those layers polished off, which removes most of the nutrients and raises the glycemic response.

name: riz précuit
description_en: Rice pre-cooked and dried for speed. The processing costs some vitamins and raises the glycemic response compared with regular rice, though parboiled versions retain more nutrients.

name: vermicelles de blé
description_en: Thin noodles made from refined wheat flour. Convenient and quick to cook, but a refined carbohydrate with little fibre unless made from whole grain.

name: quinoa
description_en: Complete amino acids, magnesium, and iron in quinoa support muscle function and oxygen transport.

name: orge
description_en: Barley’s beta-glucan fiber helps control cholesterol and supports gut health with a low glycemic response.

name: sarrasin
description_en: Buckwheat supplies rutin, magnesium, and complete plant protein for blood sugar stability and heart health.

name: epeautre
description_en: Higher protein and minerals in spelt support muscle and bone health and may aid digestion.

name: amidon de ble
description_en: Wheat starch separated from the protein and bran of the grain. It behaves like a fast sugar in the body, with little nutritional value — the whole grain is always the better option.

name: fécule de pomme de terre
description_en: Potato starch extracted industrially. Gluten-free and thickening, but a refined carbohydrate stripped of the potato’s fibre and potassium.

name: farine de riz
description_en: Milled white rice, naturally gluten-free and easy to digest. With the bran and germ removed it behaves like a fast sugar in the body, so wholegrain rice flour is the better option.

name: fecule de tapioca
description_en: Starch extracted from the cassava root. It is naturally gluten-free and useful as a thickener, but like every isolated starch it is a refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic response and none of the fibre or minerals of the root.

name: farine de mais
description_en: Corn milled into flour or semolina. Unlike cornstarch it keeps part of the grain's protein and fibre, but its glycemic index stays high once cooked. Naturally gluten-free.

name: fécule de maïs
description_en: Cornstarch extracted industrially, often from GM corn outside the EU. A refined carbohydrate with a high glycemic index and no fibre, vitamins or minerals.

name: vinaigre
description_en: Acetic acid in vinegar helps lower blood sugar response and enhances flavor without salt.

name: huile d'olive
description_en: Olive oil is a basic culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and antioxidant polyphenols, benefiting cardiovascular health.

name: huile de coco
description_en: Medium-chain fats in coconut oil provide a stable cooking fat source when used moderately.
aliases: huile de noix de coco vierge
huile de coco pressee a froid
huile de coco pressée à froid

name: huile d'avocat
description_en: Avocado oil is a simple culinary fat rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E, stable for cooking due to its high smoke point.

name: huile de lin
description_en: Flaxseed oil offers omega-3 ALA that supports heart and brain health when used raw.

name: huile de noix
description_en: Walnut oil supplies omega-3 ALA and polyphenols that support cardiovascular health.

name: huile de sesame
description_en: Sesame oil contains antioxidants that protect cells and remain stable during cooking.

name: beurre
description_en: Butter provides natural saturated fat that should be consumed in moderation.

name: creme
description_en: Dairy fat in cream offers energy but should be consumed in moderation due to saturated fat.

name: lait
description_en: Complete protein, calcium, iodine, and B12 in milk support bone health and energy metabolism.

name: lait ecreme
description_en: Skimmed milk provides protein, calcium, and B vitamins while reducing fat intake.

name: yaourt
description_en: Yoghurt supplies beneficial bacteria that improve digestion and gut health.

name: fromage
description_en: Concentrated protein and calcium in cheese support muscle and bone strength when eaten in moderation.

name: oeuf
description_en: High-quality protein, choline, vitamin D, B12, and lutein in eggs support brain, bone, and eye health.

name: blanc d'oeuf
description_en: Egg white, a natural ingredient from eggs.

name: whey
description_en: Whey provides complete protein and essential amino acids for muscle repair and growth.

name: petit-lait en poudre
description_en: Whey dried by high-temperature spray-drying, then used as a cheap source of protein, lactose and texture. It keeps most of whey's nutrients, but it is a dried, fractioned dairy ingredient and is high in lactose.

name: bœuf
description_en: Red meat provides complete protein, heme iron, zinc, and vitamin B12, best eaten fresh.

name: poulet
description_en: Lean poultry provides complete protein and B vitamins for muscle repair and energy metabolism.

name: levure
description_en: Baker's yeast adds B vitamins and protein while naturally raising dough without chemicals.

name: bicarbonate
description_en: Baking soda is a simple, effective raising agent free from aluminium additives.

name: ferments lactiques
description_en: Lactic acid bacteria improve digestion and support a balanced gut microbiome.

name: cacao
description_en: Flavanol-rich cocoa supports vascular health and supplies magnesium and iron.

name: beurre de cacao
description_en: Cocoa butter is a stable natural fat that distinguishes real chocolate from vegetable fat products.

name: pate de cacao
description_en: Cocoa mass retains flavanols, fiber, and minerals that support heart health and antioxidant protection.

name: chocolat noir
description_en: Dark chocolate with high cocoa content supplies flavanols and minerals that support heart and brain health.

name: chocolat non sucre
description_en: Unsweetened chocolate is rich in flavanols, magnesium, and fiber, which benefit heart and digestive health.

name: noisette
description_en: Vitamin E, monounsaturated fat, and manganese in hazelnuts support skin health and metabolism.

name: amande
description_en: Almonds supply vitamin E, magnesium, fiber, and healthy fats that support heart health.

name: noix
description_en: Source of omega-3 ALA, protein and minerals that support heart and brain health.

name: noix de cajou
description_en: Rich in magnesium, zinc and healthy fats that support heart and immune health.

name: graines
description_en: Mixed seeds provide plant protein, fiber, minerals, and healthy fats for nutrition.

name: graines de chia
description_en: Chia seeds offer soluble fiber and omega-3 ALA to aid digestion and fullness.

name: graines de lin
description_en: Flax seeds are rich in omega-3 ALA and lignans that support heart and hormonal health.

name: graines de tournesol
description_en: Sunflower seeds deliver vitamin E, magnesium, and selenium to support antioxidant defenses.

name: graines de sesame
description_en: Sesame seeds provide calcium, magnesium, and lignans that promote bone and heart health.

name: lentilles
description_en: Lentils provide plant protein, iron, folate, and fiber, supporting blood and digestive health.

name: pois chiches
description_en: Protein, fiber, and slow carbs in chickpeas promote fullness and support stable blood sugar levels.

name: proteine de pois chiche
description_en: Protein milled and water-separated from chickpeas. It supplies plant protein, fibre and iron with a milder taste than yellow pea protein, but it remains a fractioned ingredient rather than the whole pulse.

name: farine de pois
description_en: Dried yellow peas simply milled into flour, with no chemical extraction. Unlike a protein isolate it keeps the whole pea's fibre and starch, making it one of the least processed plant-protein ingredients.

name: haricots
description_en: Rich in plant protein and fiber, haricots support stable blood sugar levels.

name: tofu
description_en: Provides complete plant protein, calcium, and isoflavones for bone and muscle health.

name: fruit
description_en: Whole fruits and vegetables provide fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants that promote overall health.

name: pomme
description_en: Rich in fibre and antioxidants, which slow sugar absorption and support heart health.

name: tomate
description_en: Cooking increases lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart and skin health.

name: carotte
description_en: Carrots provide beta-carotene for vitamin A and fiber, aiding vision and digestion.

name: epinard
description_en: Folate, vitamin K, magnesium, and iron in spinach support blood health and vision.

name: brocoli
description_en: Broccoli's vitamin C, K, fibre, and sulforaphane support immune health and cellular protection.

name: chou
description_en: Cabbage is high in vitamins C and K and fiber, supporting immune function and gut health.

name: raisin
description_en: Polyphenols and fiber in grapes help moderate blood sugar and provide antioxidant protection.

name: fraise
description_en: High in vitamin C and antioxidants, berries help protect cells and support immune health.

name: fibre de racine de manioc
description_en: Cassava root fiber feeds beneficial gut bacteria and supports digestive health.

name: mais déshydraté
description_en: Whole dried corn supplies fiber, B vitamins, and carotenoids, promoting digestion and nutrition.

name: oignon déshydraté
description_en: Keeps part of the onion's antioxidants while seasoning food naturally.

name: poudre de celeri
description_en: Celery stalk or celeriac, simply dried and ground - harmless as a seasoning. Worth knowing, though, that the meat industry uses celery powder and celery juice as a natural nitrate source to cure meat labelled "no nitrites added": the body converts that nitrate to nitrite and the same nitroso-compounds form. On a charcuterie label it is a curing agent, not a vegetable.

name: gingembre
description_en: Anti-inflammatory gingerols in ginger help reduce nausea and support digestive health.

name: curcuma
description_en: Curcumin in turmeric helps reduce inflammation when absorbed properly with fat and black pepper.

name: cannelle
description_en: Cinnamon helps regulate blood sugar, with Ceylon cinnamon preferred for regular use.

name: vanille
description_en: Vanilla is a natural plant flavoring used in tiny amounts, with no additives or identified risks, distinct from synthetic vanillin.

name: poivre
description_en: Antioxidant-rich spices and herbs enhance flavor while reducing the need for added salt.

name: ail
description_en: Garlic is a whole, unprocessed food containing sulfur compounds with antibacterial properties and beneficial effects on blood pressure.

name: oignon
description_en: Quercetin, sulfur compounds, and prebiotic fructans in onion support antioxidant defenses and gut health.

name: echalote
description_en: Small bulb from the onion family with a milder taste, eaten fresh.

name: epices
description_en: Natural spices, herbs and seasonings are healthy and rich in antioxidants.

name: sucre de fleur de coco
description_en: A natural sugar from coconut flower sap.

name: miel
description_en: Raw honey brings antioxidants, enzymes and antibacterial compounds that refined sugar does not have. It is still around 80% sugar, and the WHO counts it as a free sugar exactly like table sugar - a better sweetener, not a free one. Never give honey to a baby under one year old, because of the risk of infant botulism.

name: sirop d'erable
description_en: Maple syrup is simply concentrated maple sap, and it carries manganese, zinc and polyphenols that refining would remove. It is nonetheless about two thirds sugar and counts as a free sugar in dietary guidelines - a whole-food sweetener to use sparingly.

name: sucre de dattes
description_en: Date sugar is a natural sweetener made by grinding dried dates, retaining fiber, potassium, magnesium, and antioxidants.

name: sirop d'érable déshydraté
description_en: Dehydrated maple syrup retains natural antioxidants and minerals, serving as an unrefined natural sugar alternative.

name: erythritol
description_en: A polyol sweetener produced by fermentation. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2023 and, for the first time ever, set an ADI based on an immediate effect - diarrhoea - at 0.5 g/kg body weight per day, then concluded that both acute and chronic intake exceed that ADI in every age group. Separate Cleveland Clinic work links circulating erythritol to platelet reactivity and cardiovascular events; that is association plus mechanism rather than proof, but it is enough to set it apart from older polyols.

name: stevia leaf
description_en: Whole stevia leaf provides sweetness without calories or blood sugar impact.

name: xylitol
description_en: A polyol sweetener used in sugar-free gum, sweets and drinks. It is dose-dependently laxative, and a 2024 European Heart Journal study linked circulating xylitol to major cardiovascular events and showed heightened platelet reactivity in every volunteer after ingestion. The evidence is associative plus mechanistic rather than causal, but it places xylitol alongside erythritol rather than with the other polyols.

name: rebaudioside m
description_en: A steviol glycoside with a cleaner taste than earlier stevia extracts, now often produced by fermentation rather than leaf extraction. It is approved and calorie-free, but industrially manufactured.

name: vitamine c
description_en: E300, known as ascorbic acid, helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports immune health.

name: pectine
description_en: E440, or pectin, benefits digestive health by promoting gut flora balance and regularity.

name: lecithine de tournesol
description_en: A natural emulsifier pressed from sunflower seeds, used to blend fat and water. Unlike soy lecithin it is obtained mechanically rather than with solvents, involves no GM crop and carries no soy allergen - which makes it the cleanest emulsifier commonly found on a label.

name: agar agar
description_en: E406, agar-agar, supports digestive health as a source of dietary fiber.

name: the vert
description_en: Offers antioxidants and gentle caffeine with calming L-theanine effects.

name: the noir
description_en: Supplies antioxidants and moderate caffeine for alertness and protection.

name: cafe
description_en: Coffee delivers antioxidants and is linked to lower risks of type 2 diabetes and liver disease.

name: cafeine
description_en: Caffeine boosts alertness and physical performance but can disrupt sleep and should be limited in pregnancy.

name: guarana
description_en: Natural caffeine in guarana provides sustained energy without rapid spikes.

name: theine
description_en: Contains natural stimulants that provide longer-lasting, milder energy than coffee.

name: l-theanine
description_en: L-theanine promotes calm alertness and reduces caffeine-induced jitteriness.

name: taurine
description_en: An amino acid the body produces naturally, added in large amounts to energy drinks. EFSA found no safety concern for taurine itself; the real issue is the caffeine and sugar it is usually paired with.

name: ginseng
description_en: An Asian root traditionally used against fatigue, sold today mostly as a concentrated extract. It is not inert: it interacts with anticoagulants and diabetes medication, can disturb sleep at higher doses, and is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

name: saumon sauvage
description_en: Wild salmon provides omega-3 EPA and DHA for brain and heart function, along with vitamin D and astaxanthin. It is leaner than farmed salmon and free of the feed, treatments and added colourants of aquaculture.

name: orange
description_en: Vitamin C, fiber, and flavonoids in whole oranges support immunity and improve iron absorption.

name: peche
description_en: Stone fruits supply fiber, potassium, carotenoids, and anti-inflammatory compounds for overall health.

name: mure
description_en: Anthocyanins in dark berries support heart health and cognitive function.

name: mangue
description_en: Vitamins A and C and digestive enzymes in mango support immune health and digestion while fiber balances natural sugars.

name: noix de coco
description_en: Medium-chain saturated fats in coconut provide energy and support metabolism when consumed in moderation.

name: avocat
description_en: Monounsaturated fats and vitamin E in avocado support heart health and improve absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

name: figue
description_en: Dried figs provide fiber and minerals that support digestion and heart health.

name: datte
description_en: Rich in fibre, potassium and natural sugars — a nutritious energy source in moderation.

name: raisin sec
description_en: Raisins are rich in antioxidants and fiber, aiding digestion and heart health.

name: cranberries sechees
description_en: Dried cranberries supply vitamins and antioxidants that help maintain urinary tract health.

name: grenade
description_en: Pomegranate seeds are dense in punicalagins and anthocyanins, among the most concentrated antioxidants in any fruit, along with fibre and vitamin K.

name: rhubarbe
description_en: Rhubarb stalks are very low in sugar and high in fibre and vitamin K, which makes them one of the few fruits used in desserts that adds almost no sweetness of its own. Only the stalk is edible: the leaves contain enough oxalic acid to be genuinely toxic and must never be eaten.

name: plantain
description_en: Plantain is a starchy banana always eaten cooked. Green plantain is high in resistant starch, which feeds gut bacteria and blunts the glycemic response; as it ripens that starch turns to sugar.

name: pomme de terre
description_en: Rich in potassium, vitamin C and fibre when the skin is kept on - a genuinely nutritious whole vegetable. Two things to know: potatoes that have turned green or sprouted accumulate solanine, which is bitter and toxic, so those parts should be cut away generously; and frying or roasting at high heat is what generates acrylamide.

name: courgette
description_en: A tender summer squash eaten whole with its skin.

name: courge
description_en: Winter squashes (butternut, pumpkin, patty pan) eaten cooked.

name: concombre
description_en: A fruit-vegetable made of more than 95% water, eaten raw.

name: cornichon
description_en: A small cucumber preserved in a heavily salted vinegar brine. Rated occasional because the base vegetable is healthy, but curing loads it with sodium and industrial versions often add preservatives and colourings. Use it as a condiment, not as a vegetable portion.

name: aubergine
description_en: A fruit-vegetable with spongy flesh, always eaten cooked.

name: poivron
description_en: A sweet pepper eaten raw or cooked, red, yellow or green depending on ripeness.

name: piment
description_en: Chillies contain capsaicin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects at culinary doses.

name: chou-fleur
description_en: Cruciferous vegetables provide fiber, vitamin C, and glucosinolates, aiding digestion and antioxidant protection.

name: salade
description_en: Raw lettuce leaves (romaine, iceberg, frisée, escarole).

name: roquette
description_en: A young peppery leaf from the brassica family.

name: mache
description_en: A small winter salad with tender leaves, eaten raw.

name: cresson
description_en: An aquatic plant with pungent leaves, from the brassica family.

name: endive
description_en: A chicory bud grown in darkness, eaten raw or braised.

name: celeri
description_en: Rich in fibre and potassium, which support digestion and heart health.

name: poireau
