description_en: Prebiotic fiber and antibacterial sulfur compounds in leeks nourish gut bacteria and help fight infections.

name: petits pois
description_en: Pulses provide plant protein, fiber, and slow carbohydrates that improve blood sugar and cholesterol levels.

name: champignon
description_en: Mushrooms provide B vitamins, selenium, beta-glucans, and vitamin D, supporting immunity and bone health.

name: okra
description_en: Okra provides soluble fibre that helps regulate blood sugar and cholesterol, with very few calories. Its mucilage is what thickens stews and gumbo.

name: millet
description_en: Small whole grains that are naturally gluten-free (millet, sorghum, teff, fonio).

name: amarante
description_en: Amaranth is a South American pseudo-cereal rich in complete protein, iron, and magnesium, and contains no gluten.

name: kamut
description_en: Kamut is an ancient durum wheat variety richer in protein and selenium than modern wheat, but contains gluten.

name: seigle
description_en: A hardy cereal used as grain or flour, notably for dark bread.

name: son d'avoine
description_en: Oat bran is the outer layer of the oat grain, very rich in beta-glucans that help lower cholesterol.

name: son de blé
description_en: Wheat bran is the husk of the wheat grain, highly concentrated in insoluble fiber useful for intestinal transit.

name: germe de blé
description_en: Wheat germ is the embryo of the wheat grain, rich in vitamin E, magnesium, zinc, and B vitamins.

name: boulgour
description_en: Durum wheat steamed, dried and cracked, a traditional Middle Eastern method.

name: couscous
description_en: Durum wheat semolina made by removing the bran and germ from the grain. Rated occasional because it is a refined cereal: the starch remains, but the fibre and part of the minerals are lost, which raises the glycemic index. Prefer wholemeal versions when available.

name: polenta
description_en: Corn semolina, usually degermed, cooked into a porridge. Rated occasional because degerming removes the grain's fibre and healthy fats, leaving a starch with a high glycemic index. Gluten-free and additive-free, but best paired with vegetables and protein.

name: gruau
description_en: A porridge of oat flakes cooked in liquid.

name: muesli
description_en: A mix of cereal flakes, dried fruit and seeds. Rated occasional because the base is healthy, but most commercial blends add sugar, syrup or refined oils. Read the label: a muesli with no added sugar remains an excellent breakfast.

name: flocons de quinoa
description_en: Whole grains simply passed between two rollers to flatten them.

name: pates completes
description_en: Whole grain pasta offers fiber and minerals while lowering blood sugar spikes when cooked al dente.

name: riz basmati
description_en: Basmati rice has a lower glycemic index and pigmented varieties add antioxidants and fiber.

name: mouton
description_en: Mutton and similar unprocessed meats provide complete protein, iron, and B vitamins, and are generally leaner.

name: foie
description_en: Exceptionally rich in vitamin A, B12, iron and copper - one of the most nutrient-dense foods there is. Its preformed vitamin A is so concentrated that health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid liver and liver products entirely, and a single weekly portion is enough for everyone else.

name: cabillaud
description_en: Lean white fish provide complete protein, iodine, selenium and B12 with very little fat, and sit among the lowest-mercury species there are - which is why the FDA and EPA place them on the Best Choices list, two to three servings a week.

name: crevette
description_en: Shellfish supply high-quality protein, zinc, selenium, iodine and vitamin B12 for very little fat. Two practical points: crustaceans and molluscs are among the allergens the EU requires to be declared, and reactions to them are often severe; and raw oysters and clams carry a norovirus and vibrio risk, which is why they are not advised during pregnancy.

name: algue
description_en: Seaweed provides iodine, iron, magnesium and soluble fibre, supporting thyroid function and overall nutrition. Nori and wakame are moderate, but kombu is by far the most iodine-dense food known and can disturb thyroid function if eaten regularly - health agencies advise limiting it, and using it for stock rather than eating it.

name: caviar
description_en: Fish roe is rich in omega-3 EPA and DHA, vitamin B12 and vitamin D. It is also salted heavily to preserve it, which makes it one of the saltiest foods on a table - it works as a delicacy in small spoonfuls, not as a portion.

name: ricotta
description_en: Lower fat and salt in ricotta cheese make it a lighter source of calcium and protein.

name: feta
description_en: Protein and calcium in feta support muscle function and bone strength.

name: brie
description_en: Soft ripened cheeses provide calcium, protein and vitamin B12, and develop their character through surface moulds. Because their moisture and low acidity suit listeria, health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid soft ripened cheeses unless they are made from pasteurised milk or have been cooked until steaming hot.

name: roquefort
description_en: Blue cheeses concentrate calcium, protein and B12, and their moulds give them their character. They are among the saltiest cheeses there are, and health agencies advise pregnant women to avoid blue-veined cheese unless it has been cooked until steaming hot.

name: comté
description_en: Hard cooked-curd cheeses, aged for several months in wheels.

name: cantal
description_en: Cantal cheese supplies calcium and protein, contributing to strong bones and muscle maintenance.

name: reblochon
description_en: Reblochon cheese offers fats and salt that provide energy and support cellular functions when consumed moderately.

name: crottin
description_en: Crottin goat cheese is lower in fat and easier to digest, benefiting those sensitive to cow milk.

name: gouda
description_en: Gouda cheese delivers protein and calcium, essential for bone strength and muscle repair.

name: kefir
description_en: Fermented dairy like kefir delivers live cultures and protein for gut and muscle health.

name: ghee
description_en: Ghee is a stable cooking fat that is lactose-free and provides energy from saturated fat.

name: lait de chevre
description_en: Smaller fat globules in goat, sheep and buffalo milk may make them easier to digest for some people. Nutritionally they are close to cow's milk, with slightly more medium-chain fats.

name: lait d'amande
description_en: Plant drinks are a good dairy alternative when the ingredient list is short: water, the nut or grain, and nothing else. Most supermarket versions add sugar, oils, gums and emulsifiers, and many contain only 2 to 3% almond, which leaves a drink with almost no protein. Choose unsweetened and fortified with calcium.

name: noix du bresil
description_en: The richest natural source of selenium on the planet, which supports thyroid function and antioxidant defences. One or two nuts already cover a full day's requirement, and eating them by the handful every day can exceed the tolerable upper intake - a rare case where a whole food needs a portion limit.

name: noix de pecan
description_en: Pecan nuts provide healthy fats and antioxidants that support heart and brain health.

name: noix de macadamia
description_en: Macadamia nuts supply monounsaturated fats that help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

name: pignon de pin
description_en: Pine nuts offer essential fatty acids and vitamins that contribute to energy production and immune function.

name: noix de pili
description_en: A buttery tree nut rich in magnesium and healthy fats that support heart health.

name: chataigne
description_en: Chestnuts are rich in fiber and vitamin C, aiding digestion and immune defense.

name: arachide
description_en: A good source of plant protein, fibre and heart-healthy fats.

name: beurre de cacahuete
description_en: Peanut butter is rich in good fats, fiber, magnesium, and vitamin E, supporting cardiovascular health.

name: graines de courge
description_en: Pumpkin and other seeds supply minerals, protein, and healthy fats for body functions.

name: coriandre
description_en: Concentrated antioxidants and essential oils in fresh herbs support overall health without added salt or sugar.

name: cardamome
description_en: The dried pod of a plant in the ginger family, used whole or ground.

name: clou de girofle
description_en: The dried flower bud of the clove tree, used whole or ground.

name: noix de muscade
description_en: Nutmeg is a spice used in small amounts that adds flavor without nutritional risk at culinary doses.

name: anis
description_en: Green anise seeds or the dried fruit of star anise.

name: fenugrec
description_en: A dried legume seed, used ground in curries.

name: safran
description_en: Saffron is a natural plant-based coloring and flavoring that does not affect nutrition when used sparingly.

name: sumac
description_en: Dried, ground berries from a Mediterranean shrub, with a tangy taste.

name: zaatar
description_en: Zaatar benefits the body by providing natural herbs and spices rich in antioxidants and nutrients.

name: curry
description_en: Curry benefits the body by supplying curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory properties.

name: sichuan pepper
description_en: The dried berry of a Chinese prickly ash, botanically unrelated to pepper.

name: poivre noir
description_en: Peppercorns harvested at different stages and dried (black, white, green).

name: poivre rose
description_en: Poivre rose benefits the body as a mild, resinous dried berry with no additives.

name: poivre de cayenne
description_en: Red chillies dried and ground into a fine powder.

name: piment de la jamaique
description_en: The dried berry of the pimento tree, whose aroma recalls clove, cinnamon and nutmeg at once.

name: piment fumé
description_en: Natural spice/herb with antioxidants and anti-inflammatory compounds.

name: feuille de kaffir
description_en: Aromatic leaves and rhizomes used fresh in South-East Asian cooking - kaffir lime leaf, lemongrass, galangal, fresh turmeric, ginger root and curry leaf. They are whole plant parts, used in small amounts, and carry the essential oils and antioxidants of the fresh plant.

name: herbes de provence
description_en: Blends of dried aromatic herbs (thyme, rosemary, savory, bay).

name: persillade
description_en: Preparations of fresh chopped herbs with garlic, zest or olive oil.

name: moutarde
description_en: Mustard is simply crushed mustard seed with vinegar and salt. It adds flavour for almost no calories and keeps the antioxidant compounds of the seed. Dijon and wholegrain versions contain little beyond seed, vinegar, water and salt.

name: harissa
description_en: A paste of crushed red chillies with garlic, coriander and cumin, a North African speciality.

name: sambal
description_en: Sambal benefits the body by offering fermented or crushed vegetables with natural flavors.

name: pâte de piment
description_en: Fresh or dried chillies crushed with salt, sometimes oil or vinegar.

name: pâte de curry
description_en: Pâte de curry benefits the body by delivering fresh crushed plants rich in natural compounds.

name: pesto
description_en: Pesto benefits the body by combining whole foods like basil, pine nuts, and olive oil for nutrients.

name: tapenade
description_en: Black or green olives crushed with capers, anchovies and olive oil.

name: pâte d'anchois
description_en: Salted anchovies reduced to a paste, sometimes with a little oil.

name: humus maison
description_en: Cooked chickpeas blended with tahini, olive oil, lemon and garlic - plant protein, fibre, unsaturated fat and calcium in one spread. Homemade versions contain nothing else; industrial tubs often add preservatives and cheaper oils.

name: cornichon naturel
description_en: Vegetables preserved by lacto-fermentation in brine rather than vinegar. Live bacteria and organic acids survive in the jar as long as it has not been pasteurised, which supports gut flora. The salt in the brine is the only thing to keep an eye on.

name: sirop de yacon
description_en: Syrup from the yacon root, unusual in that most of its sweetness comes from fructo-oligosaccharides that the body does not absorb, so it feeds gut bacteria instead of raising blood sugar. Large amounts cause bloating for the same reason.

name: fruit du moine
description_en: A sweetener from the luo han guo fruit, with no calories and no effect on blood sugar. It has a long history of use in Asia and is widely permitted in North America. In the EU only an aqueous decoction of the fruit has been authorised, while purified mogroside V - the form used in most imported products - is still awaiting authorisation.

name: allulose
description_en: A rare sugar that sweetens with almost no calories and no effect on blood glucose. It is authorised in the United States, Canada, Japan and Korea, but not in the European Union or the UK, where it is still going through novel food assessment. Large amounts cause bloating and digestive upset.

name: levain
description_en: A natural starter of wild yeasts and lactic bacteria. Long sourdough fermentation breaks down part of the gluten and the phytates that block mineral absorption, which makes sourdough bread more digestible and its magnesium, zinc and iron more available than in yeasted bread.

name: pain complet
description_en: Whole grain breads provide high fiber and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

name: couscous complet
description_en: Whole grains provide fibre and minerals for sustained energy and digestive health.

name: eau de source
description_en: Drinking water from a spring or simply filtered, with nothing added.

name: tisane
description_en: An infusion of dried plants, flowers or fruit in hot water, caffeine-free.

name: thé blanc
description_en: Young tea buds simply withered and dried, without oxidation.

name: thé oolong
description_en: Teas that are partially oxidised (oolong) or fermented and aged (pu-erh).

name: matcha
description_en: Green tea leaves grown in the shade then ground whole into powder.

name: maté
description_en: A traditional South American infusion of dried yerba mate leaves. Rated occasional because the plant is natural, but IARC classifies drinking mate very hot (above 65 °C) as probably carcinogenic to the oesophagus — the temperature is the issue, not the plant. Drinking it warm removes that risk.

name: hibiscus
description_en: An infusion of dried hibiscus flowers, tart and bright red.

name: camomille
description_en: An infusion of dried chamomile flowers, caffeine-free.

name: chicoree torrefiee
description_en: Chicory root dried then roasted, drunk as a coffee substitute.

name: jus de fruits frais
description_en: Freshly pressed juice keeps the vitamins and polyphenols of the fruit, but pressing removes the fibre that slows sugar absorption. The WHO counts fruit juice as a free sugar for that reason, and a glass concentrates the sugar of several pieces of fruit. Whole fruit is always the better version; vegetable-based juices avoid most of the issue.

name: chlorella
description_en: A freshwater microalga dried into powder or tablets, rich in protein, iron and chlorophyll. Because it absorbs what its growing water contains, the quality of sourcing decides whether it also carries heavy metals - certified production matters more here than for most foods.

name: maca
description_en: An Andean root dried then ground, eaten as a food in Peru for centuries.

name: ashwagandha
description_en: A dried Ayurvedic root, sold as powder or concentrated extract. Rated occasional because the plant is natural, but concentrated supplements are not advised in pregnancy and several European agencies have reported cases of liver injury. Use occasionally, not continuously.

name: reishi
description_en: Medicinal mushrooms sold as dried powder or concentrated extract. They supply beta-glucans and are well tolerated as a food. As a supplement, reishi has been associated with rare cases of liver injury - the NIH LiverTox database describes clinically apparent injury as extremely rare, and reported cases mostly involve the unextracted powdered form, alcohol use or existing liver disease. It can also interact with anticoagulants. Treat it as a supplement with its own precautions, not as an ordinary mushroom.

name: baobab
description_en: The pulp of the baobab fruit, naturally dry and simply sieved into powder.

name: moringa
description_en: Moringa leaves provide concentrated protein, calcium, iron, and vitamin A, supporting overall nutritional health.

name: caroube
description_en: Carob pod dried, roasted then ground, used as a cocoa alternative.

name: cacao cru
description_en: Cocoa beans fermented, dried and cracked, with no added sugar.

name: gelee royale
description_en: Bee products carrying enzymes, amino acids and antibacterial compounds. They are also documented allergens: royal jelly and propolis have caused severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis, rare but well recorded, and are best avoided by people with asthma or a known allergy to bee products. Pollen can trigger reactions in people allergic to the source plants.

name: huile de chanvre
description_en: Cold-pressed virgin oils, rich in omega-3 and essential fatty acids.

name: vinaigre de riz
description_en: Acidity from rice vinegar aids digestion and enhances flavor without added chemicals.

name: 된장
description_en: Traditional Korean fermented soybean paste, rich in probiotics and enzymes.

name: gochujang
description_en: A Korean fermented paste of chilli, glutinous rice and soybeans. The traditional version is a genuine ferment; most supermarket jars list glucose-fructose syrup among the main ingredients, which puts them closer to a sweet sauce than to a ferment. The ingredient list decides which one you have.

name: 고춧가루
description_en: Korean red pepper powder, a simple dried and ground spice.

name: 국간장
description_en: Korean soup soy sauce from traditional meju fermentation.

name: 간장
description_en: 간장 is Korean brewed soy sauce traditionally fermented; brewed versions are preferable to chemically acid-hydrolyzed ones.

name: 쌈장
description_en: 쌈장 is a Korean condiment blending doenjang and gochujang with a naturally fermented base.

name: 청국장
description_en: Cheonggukjang is rich in probiotics that support gut health and digestion.

name: 메주
description_en: Fermented soybean block, the traditional base of doenjang and ganjang.

name: 액젓
description_en: Korean fermented fish sauce (anchovy or sand lance).

name: jeotgal
description_en: Seafood salted and fermented for months, used as a seasoning and as a base for kimchi. It is a genuine traditional ferment, and it is also preserved in enough salt to make it one of the highest-sodium foods in any cuisine - a condiment by the spoonful, never a portion.

name: kimchi
description_en: Lacto-fermented vegetables rich in live lactic bacteria, fibre, vitamin C and beta-carotene - one of the best-studied traditional ferments there is. Its one drawback is salt: kimchi is brined, and diets very high in salted foods are an established risk factor for stomach cancer, so it works best as a side dish rather than a main portion.

name: 참기름
description_en: Pressed toasted sesame oil, rich in antioxidants (sesamol).

name: 들기름
description_en: Pressed perilla oil, very rich in omega-3 (alpha-linolenic acid).

name: 미숫가루
description_en: Korean roasted grain and legume powder.

name: thaumatine
description_en: A sweet protein (E957) extracted from the West African katemfe fruit, around 2,000 times sweeter than sugar. It is plant-derived and digested like any protein, but it is a concentrated industrial extract with a lingering liquorice aftertaste.

name: neohesperidine dc
description_en: A synthetic sweetener (E959) derived from bitter orange peel, several hundred times sweeter than sugar. It is authorised in the EU but not in the United States, and is used mainly to mask bitterness in industrial products.

name: neotame
description_en: An artificial sweetener (E961) built from aspartame, up to 13,000 times sweeter than sugar. EFSA re-evaluated it in 2025 and found no safety concern at permitted levels, though the WHO advises against sweeteners for weight control.

name: sel d aspartame acesulfame
description_en: A combined salt of aspartame and acesulfame K (E962), used to balance the aftertaste of each. It carries the concerns of both parent sweeteners, including aspartame's IARC Group 2B classification.

name: advantame
description_en: An artificial sweetener (E969) derived from aspartame and roughly 37,000 times sweeter than sugar, so it is used in minute amounts. Authorised in the EU and US, but a purely synthetic high-intensity sweetener.

name: sirop de polyglycitol
description_en: A polyol syrup (E964) made by hydrogenating starch, used as a bulk sweetener in sugar-free products. Like all polyols it is poorly absorbed and carries a mandatory laxative warning above 10%.

name: methylcellulose
description_en: A chemically modified cellulose (E461) used to thicken and bind, notably in plant-based meat substitutes. It is not absorbed and passes through as fibre, but it is a laboratory-modified ingredient.

name: ethylcellulose
description_en: A modified cellulose (E462) used as a binder and film former. It is indigestible and considered safe, serving a purely technical role in manufacturing.

name: phosphate de monoamidon
description_en: A modified starch (E1410) used to thicken and stabilise processed food. EFSA considers modified starches safe, but they are refined carbohydrates and a marker of ultra-processing.

name: amidon acetyle
description_en: Acetylated starch (E1420), chemically treated to stay stable through processing. It is a refined carbohydrate with no fibre or micronutrients, used purely for texture.

name: acide acetique
description_en: Vinegar acid (E260) helps preserve food and slightly lowers blood sugar response when taken with meals.

name: acetate de sodium
description_en: The sodium salt of acetic acid (E262), used as a preservative and to give salt-and-vinegar flavour. It is well tolerated but contributes sodium to the diet.

name: acide fumarique
description_en: An acidity regulator (E297) that occurs naturally in plants and in human metabolism. It is considered safe at food levels, though the food-grade version is synthesised industrially.

name: ascorbate de sodium
description_en: Sodium ascorbate (E301) supports antioxidant activity and helps maintain healthy vitamin C levels in the body.

name: ascorbate de calcium
description_en: Calcium ascorbate (E302) provides vitamin C and calcium, supporting immune function and bone health.

name: palmitate d ascorbyle
description_en: A fat-soluble form of vitamin C (E304) used to keep oils from going rancid. It is broken down into vitamin C and palmitic acid in the body, and is considered safe at permitted levels.

name: lactate de sodium
description_en: The sodium salt of lactic acid (E325), used to preserve and retain moisture in meat and baked goods. It is well tolerated but adds sodium to an already salty product category.

name: lactate de potassium
description_en: A preservative and acidity regulator (E326) often used to reduce sodium in processed meat. It is considered safe, though people with kidney disease should limit added potassium salts.

name: lactate de calcium
description_en: A firming agent and acidity regulator (E327) that also supplies calcium. It is well tolerated and one of the more benign mineral salts used in food.

name: acide adipique
description_en: An acidity regulator (E355) used in powdered desserts and drink mixes. It is produced industrially and considered safe at the low levels permitted.

name: acide alginique
description_en: A gelling fibre (E400) extracted from brown seaweed. It is not absorbed and behaves as soluble fibre, though large amounts can reduce mineral absorption.

name: alginate de propylene glycol
description_en: A chemically modified alginate (E405) used to stabilise beer foam and dressings. Unlike plain alginates it is reacted with propylene glycol, making it a synthetic derivative rather than a simple seaweed extract.

name: eucheuma transforme
description_en: Processed eucheuma seaweed (E407a), a cheaper, less purified relative of carrageenan. It shares carrageenan's concerns about gut inflammation and is banned in EU infant formula.

name: gomme adragante
description_en: A plant gum (E413) from the astragalus shrub, used as a thickener and stabiliser. It behaves as soluble fibre and is well tolerated, though it can cause bloating in quantity.

name: gomme cassia
description_en: A thickener (E427) from cassia tree seeds, authorised in the EU with strict purity limits because the raw seed contains natural anthraquinones. Purified food grade is considered safe.

name: phosphatides d ammonium
description_en: An emulsifier (E442) used almost exclusively in chocolate to control flow during moulding. It is authorised at low levels but is a synthetic phosphate derivative with no place in traditional chocolate.

name: esters de propylene glycol
description_en: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids (E477), used to aerate whipped toppings and cake mixes. Permitted at capped levels, and characteristic of ultra-processed desserts.

name: sorbitanes
description_en: Sorbitan emulsifiers (E491–E495) used to stabilise fats in baked goods and confectionery. They belong to the synthetic emulsifier family under study for effects on the gut lining.

name: dimethylpolysiloxane
description_en: A silicone anti-foaming agent (E900) used mainly in frying oils and industrial cooking. It is inert and poorly absorbed, but it is a synthetic silicone typical of large-scale food production.

name: cire de candelilla
description_en: E902 is a plant wax from a Mexican shrub that provides a vegan alternative to beeswax and shellac.

name: cire microcristalline
description_en: A petroleum-derived wax (E905) used as a glazing and release agent. It is not absorbed by the body, but it originates from mineral oil refining rather than from a plant or animal source.

name: protoxyde d azote
description_en: Nitrous oxide (E942), the propellant in aerosol whipped cream. It is inert in food use and leaves no residue, though inhaling it recreationally causes serious neurological harm.

name: polydextrose
description_en: A synthetic soluble fibre (E1200) made from glucose, used to add bulk and fibre while cutting sugar. It is largely unabsorbed and acts as a prebiotic, but large amounts cause bloating.

name: pvp
description_en: Polyvinylpyrrolidone (E1201), a synthetic polymer used to clarify drinks and coat tablets. It is not absorbed by the gut and is considered safe, serving a purely technical purpose.

name: triacetine
description_en: A humectant and solvent (E1518) used to carry flavours and keep products moist. It breaks down into glycerol and acetic acid in the body and is considered safe at food levels.

name: talc alimentaire
description_en: Food-grade talc (E553b) used to stop powders sticking and clumping. IARC reclassified talc as Group 2A, probably carcinogenic to humans, in 2024, on limited evidence in humans, sufficient evidence in animals and strong mechanistic evidence. A separate and older concern is contamination with asbestos, which occurs naturally alongside talc deposits and is a confirmed Group 1 carcinogen.

name: moah
description_en: Mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons, contaminants from packaging inks, machine lubricants and processing aids. EFSA considers those with three or more aromatic rings genotoxic and carcinogenic, and found their presence in infant formula to be of health concern.

name: mosh
description_en: Mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons, which migrate into food from packaging and machinery. EFSA concluded in 2023 that current dietary exposure raises no health concern, though they accumulate in the liver and lymphatic tissue and long-term effects remain uncertain.

name: oxyde d ethylene
description_en: A fumigant banned in EU food production and classified as mutagenic, carcinogenic and reprotoxic, with no safe level established. Its detection in imported sesame and locust bean gum triggered the largest food recall operation in EU history from 2020.

name: 2 chloroethanol
description_en: The reaction product of ethylene oxide with chloride, measured together with it under the same EU residue limit. Its own genotoxicity is debated, but its presence indicates treatment with a banned carcinogenic fumigant.

name: dioxines
description_en: Persistent industrial by-products that accumulate in animal fat and reach us mainly through meat, dairy and fish. TCDD is an IARC Group 1 human carcinogen, and EFSA cut the tolerable weekly intake sevenfold in 2018.

name: pcb
description_en: Polychlorinated biphenyls, banned industrial oils that persist for decades in the environment and concentrate in fatty fish. IARC classifies them Group 1 human carcinogens, and they are also linked to hormonal and developmental effects.

name: chlorpyrifos
description_en: An organophosphate insecticide banned across the EU since 2020. EFSA could not establish a safe exposure level, citing genotoxicity concerns and evidence of harm to brain development in children.

name: atrazine
description_en: A herbicide banned in the EU since 2004 but still detected in groundwater decades later. It is widely regarded as an endocrine disruptor affecting hormonal and reproductive function, and remains in use in North America.

name: paraquat
description_en: A herbicide banned in the EU since 2007 because of its extreme acute toxicity — a small ingested dose can be fatal with no antidote. Epidemiological studies also associate exposure with a raised risk of Parkinson's disease.

name: irradiation
description_en: Treatment with ionising radiation to kill microbes and extend shelf life. It leaves no radioactivity and is authorised in the EU for a narrow list of foods, which must carry an "irradiated" label; it does degrade some vitamins.

name: sorbitol
description_en: A polyol sweetener (E420) that is only partly absorbed, so it raises blood sugar less than sugar. EU law requires a laxative warning above 10%, as it commonly causes bloating and diarrhoea.

name: mannitol
description_en: A polyol sweetener and anti-caking agent (E421) with roughly half the calories of sugar. Like all polyols it is poorly absorbed and carries a mandatory laxative warning above 10%.

name: isomalt
description_en: A polyol (E953) made from sucrose, common in sugar-free sweets. It does not feed tooth decay and has a low glycemic impact, but it causes digestive upset in larger amounts.

name: maltitol
description_en: A polyol (E965) widely used in sugar-free chocolate. It still raises blood sugar noticeably — more than other polyols — and is one of the most likely to cause bloating and laxative effects.

name: lactitol
description_en: A polyol (E966) derived from lactose, poorly absorbed and used in sugar-free products. It reaches the colon largely intact, which is why it carries a laxative warning above 10%.

name: acide phosphorique
description_en: An acidity regulator (E338) that gives colas their sharp bite. EFSA set a combined phosphate limit of 40 mg/kg in 2019 and warned that some groups already exceed it; high phosphate intake concerns kidney and bone health.

name: esters acetiques
description_en: Acetic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472a), an emulsifier used to stabilise fats in industrial baking and desserts. EFSA raised no safety concern, but it is a purely technical ingredient.
aliases: esters acetiques des mono et diglycerides
acetic acid esters of mono and diglycerides

name: esters lactiques
description_en: Lactic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472b), used to aerate whipped and baked products. Considered safe by EFSA, it is a chemically modified fat with no nutritional role.
aliases: esters lactiques des mono et diglycerides
lactic acid esters of mono and diglycerides

name: esters citriques
description_en: Citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides (E472c), used to emulsify and prevent oxidation. EFSA found no safety concern, though it marks an industrially assembled recipe.
aliases: esters citriques des mono et diglycerides
citric acid esters of mono and diglycerides

name: datem
description_en: DATEM (E472e), a dough strengthener in industrial bread. EFSA found no safety concern in 2020, but laboratory work links it to gut microbiome disruption and a large French cohort tied higher intake to slightly raised type 2 diabetes risk.

name: esters de sucrose
description_en: Sucrose esters of fatty acids (E473), synthetic emulsifiers built from sugar and fat. They are authorised at limited levels but belong to the emulsifier family under study for effects on the gut lining.

name: esters polyglyceriques
description_en: Polyglycerol esters of fatty acids (E475), used to emulsify cakes, ice cream and spreads. Permitted at capped levels, and a clear marker of ultra-processed formulation.

name: stearoyl lactylate de sodium
description_en: Sodium stearoyl lactylate (E481), a dough conditioner that improves volume and shelf life in industrial bread. It is authorised at limited levels but never needed in traditionally made bread.

name: sels d acides gras
description_en: Fatty acid salts (E470), used as anti-caking and glazing agents rather than as a food fat. They are refined industrial derivatives typical of processed formulations.

name: acide sorbique
description_en: A mould inhibitor (E200) and one of the gentler preservatives, occurring naturally in rowan berries. It is well tolerated, though it can cause mild skin or digestive reactions in sensitive people.

name: acide propionique
description_en: A mould inhibitor (E280) used mainly in industrial bread. It occurs naturally in some cheeses and is considered safe by EFSA, but its presence signals bread built for long shelf life.

name: propionate de sodium
description_en: A bread preservative (E281) that blocks mould and rope spoilage. EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels; it marks industrial rather than fresh-baked bread.

name: natamycine
description_en: An antifungal (E235) applied to the surface of cheese and cured sausage. It is not absorbed through the gut wall, but it is an antibiotic-class compound, raising questions about resistance.

name: nisine
description_en: A natural antibacterial peptide (E234) produced by lactic bacteria, used in cheese and canned foods. It is digested like any protein and is one of the most benign preservatives available.

name: glutamate monopotassique
description_en: A flavour enhancer (E622) from the glutamate family, used like MSG to build savoury taste with less real ingredient. It is a reliable marker of ultra-processed food.

name: diglutamate de calcium
description_en: A flavour enhancer (E623) used as a lower-sodium alternative to MSG. Considered safe at food levels, but it signals a product engineered on additives rather than ingredients.

name: glutamate monoammonique
description_en: A glutamate flavour enhancer (E624) that intensifies umami in industrial seasonings. It performs the same role as MSG under a different name.

name: diglutamate de magnesium
description_en: A flavour enhancer (E625) from the glutamate family, used to boost savoury taste in processed foods. Safe at normal intake, but characteristic of heavily seasoned industrial products.

name: curcumine
description_en: The yellow pigment of turmeric (E100), used as a natural colouring. It is a plant-derived alternative to synthetic yellow dyes and raises no safety concern at food levels. The anti-inflammatory effects attributed to curcumin come from concentrated supplement doses, not from the trace amount used to colour a food.

name: riboflavine
description_en: Vitamin B2 is essential for energy production and supports healthy skin and eyes.

name: carotenes
description_en: Beta carotene (E160a) is an orange plant pigment converted to vitamin A and acts as an antioxidant.

name: lycopene
description_en: Lycopene (E160d) is the red pigment of tomatoes and a well-studied dietary antioxidant.

name: luteine
description_en: Lutein (E161b) is a yellow carotenoid from marigold and greens that supports eye health.

name: rouge de betterave
description_en: Beetroot pigment betanin offers antioxidant activity that helps protect cells from damage.

name: oxydes de fer
description_en: Mineral pigments (E172) used to colour coatings, sweets and cosmetics. They pass through the body largely unabsorbed and EFSA considers them safe, but they add no nutritional value.

name: gallates
description_en: Propyl, octyl and dodecyl gallate (E310–E312), synthetic antioxidants that stop fats going rancid. They are permitted at low levels but can trigger contact allergy and are restricted in foods for infants.

name: cire d abeille
description_en: Beeswax is a natural coating agent that is not absorbed by the body and is safe for consumption.

name: shellac
description_en: A resin (E904) secreted by the lac insect, used to glaze sweets, coffee beans and tablets. It is not absorbed, but it is of insect origin and therefore not vegetarian.

name: azote
description_en: Nitrogen gas is inert and safe, helping preserve food freshness without adding residues.

name: dioxyde de carbone
description_en: Carbon dioxide (E290) benefits the body by being inert and leaving no residues after use in food and drinks.

name: cellulose
description_en: Plant cellulose (E460), used as an anti-caking agent and bulking fibre. It is not digested and behaves as insoluble fibre, but in processed food it usually replaces real ingredients.

name: l cysteine
description_en: An amino acid (E920) used as a dough conditioner to speed up industrial bread making. Modern production is by bacterial fermentation, though it was historically extracted from feathers and hair.

name: phosphate de diamidon acetyle e1414
description_en: A doubly modified starch (E1414) built to survive heating, freezing and acidity. It adds texture and shelf life without nutrition, and signals an industrially engineered recipe.

name: phosphate de diamidon hydroxypropyle
description_en: One of the most common modified starches (E1442), used in sauces, desserts and ready meals to hold texture through heating and freezing. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation found no safety concern and set no numerical ADI, but it is a purely technical refined carbohydrate and a clear marker of ultra-processed food.

name: ferrocyanure de potassium
description_en: An anti-caking agent (E536) added to salt to keep it free-flowing. Despite the name, the cyanide is locked in a stable complex and EFSA considers it safe at permitted levels.

name: propionate de potassium
description_en: A mould inhibitor (E283) used in packaged bread and baked goods. Considered safe by EFSA, though it is only needed when bread must last far beyond its natural life.

name: patent blue v
description_en: E131 is a synthetic blue dye used only to change appearance and provide no nutritional value. People with a history of reactions to synthetic dyes should be cautious due to possible hypersensitivity.

name: green s
description_en: A synthetic green food dye used to create or intensify color. It has an acceptable daily intake, and high consumption of several colored products can increase total exposure. Health: The concern is unnecessary cumulative exposure and possible intolerance in sensitive individuals, not proven carcinogenicity.

name: brilliant black bn
description_en: E151 is a synthetic black dye used in confectionery, sauces, and decorations. Frequent consumption can increase exposure beyond intended daily use, especially in children.

name: brown ht
description_en: E155 is a synthetic brown dye used in bakery, dessert, and confectionery products. Repeated high intake from multiple colored products is a health concern, especially for children.

name: paprika extract, capsanthin and capsorubin
description_en: E160c is a concentrated red-orange color extracted from paprika and standardized for pigment strength. Quality control is important for solvent residues and purity; rare allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

name: canthaxanthin
description_en: An orange-red carotenoid color with a low acceptable daily intake. Excessive exposure can cause canthaxanthin crystals to accumulate in the retina. Health: High intake may produce retinal deposits and visual changes. This is a genuine dose-related health concern and is why use is tightly restricted.

name: calcium sorbate
description_en: A preservative deleted from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2018 because no company ever supplied the genotoxicity data EFSA had asked for - a data gap, not a proven toxicity. EFSA had already excluded it from the group ADI shared by sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202), partly because the related sodium salt tested positive for genotoxicity. It is no longer permitted in EU food.

name: calcium benzoate
description_en: E213 is a synthetic preservative that releases benzoate to slow microbial growth in acidic foods and drinks. Sensitive individuals may experience hives or asthma-like reactions, and high exposure should stay below the acceptable daily intake.

name: ethyl paraben
description_en: E214 is a synthetic paraben preservative used to prevent mold and bacterial growth, with weak hormone-like activity studied experimentally. No cancer claim is justified at authorized levels, but repeated combined exposure to parabens is a concern.

name: sodium ethyl paraben
description_en: E215 is the water-soluble sodium form of ethyl paraben, contributing to the combined paraben exposure limit. The main concern is cumulative exposure to parabens rather than immediate toxicity at permitted levels.

name: sodium propyl paraben
description_en: E217 is the sodium form of propyl paraben, no longer authorized in the EU due to uncertain reproductive toxicity safety. It should be avoided as a declared additive where unauthorized, especially due to repeated exposure concerns.

name: methyl paraben
description_en: A synthetic preservative used against molds and bacteria. It has weak biological activity in laboratory testing, but food use is regulated under a combined acceptable daily intake with ethyl paraben. Health: The practical concern is cumulative exposure from food, medicines, and personal-care products, not proven cancer from permitted food levels.

name: sodium methyl paraben
description_en: E219 is the sodium salt of methyl paraben, a synthetic preservative that dissolves easily in water. Repeated exposure from multiple sources is more relevant than a single food serving for health considerations.

name: soybean hemicellulose
description_en: E426 is a processed fiber fraction from soybeans used to thicken and stabilize food products. Residual soy proteins may affect people with severe soy allergies despite low toxicity of the additive.

name: beta-cyclodextrin
description_en: A ring-shaped carbohydrate manufactured from starch and used to trap, protect, or carry flavors and other compounds. It has a relatively low acceptable daily intake. Health: High exposure can exceed the recommended daily limit. The restriction is based on systemic effects observed at higher doses, not on a cancer classification.

name: tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
description_en: E472d are chemically modified fats used to strengthen dough and control texture in processed foods. No major disease risk is established at authorized levels, but cumulative intake and impurities are concerns.
aliases: esters tartriques de mono- et diglycérides
esters tartriques de mono et diglycerides
tartaric acid esters of mono and diglycerides

name: mixed acetic and tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
description_en: E472f is a complex emulsifier made by chemically esterifying mono- and diglycerides, enhancing dough and shelf life. Purity, tartaric-acid exposure, and frequent consumption of processed foods are health considerations.
aliases: esters acétiques et tartriques de mono- et diglycérides
esters acetiques et tartriques de mono et diglycerides
mixed acetic and tartaric acid esters of mono and diglycerides

name: sucroglycerides
description_en: Industrial emulsifiers produced by reacting sucrose with food fats. They help oil and water remain mixed and create a stable, smooth texture in highly formulated foods. Health: Some exposure scenarios may approach or exceed the group acceptable daily intake. Large amounts may also contribute to digestive discomfort.

name: potassium carbonates
description_en: Refined mineral salts used to control acidity, improve dough, or support manufacturing. They are not considered harmful at normal food levels. Health: Very high potassium intake can be dangerous for people with kidney disease or those taking medicines that raise blood potassium.

name: magnesium carbonates
description_en: E504 are refined magnesium salts used to prevent clumping and regulate acidity in foods. Large doses can cause diarrhea and abdominal cramping, but typical additive amounts are much lower.

name: hydrochloric acid
description_en: A strong processing acid used in controlled amounts to adjust pH or manufacture ingredients. It is neutralized or highly diluted in the finished food. Health: The concentrated industrial chemical is corrosive, but that hazard should not be confused with properly controlled residues in food.

name: calcium chloride
description_en: E509 is a refined calcium salt used to firm vegetables, set cheese, and stabilize texture. High concentrations may irritate the digestive tract and taste bitter, but normal use is not a major health concern.

name: magnesium chloride
description_en: E511 is a refined magnesium salt used in tofu, mineral fortification, and texture control. Large amounts may cause diarrhea, nausea, or abdominal cramping, especially with reduced kidney function.

name: stannous chloride
description_en: A tin compound used mainly to preserve color in a limited number of canned foods. It requires strict concentration limits. Health: Excess inorganic tin can cause acute nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. This is the principal established health concern.

name: sulfuric acid
description_en: A strong industrial acid used in controlled food processing and pH adjustment. It is neutralized or diluted before the food is consumed. Health: Concentrated sulfuric acid is severely corrosive, but properly manufactured food should not retain that corrosive hazard.

name: sodium sulfates
description_en: E514 consists of refined sulfate salts used for processing and acidity control; large doses can cause diarrhea by drawing water into the intestine. Sodium-containing forms also contribute to total sodium intake.

name: potassium sulfates
description_en: E515 is a refined potassium salt used to regulate acidity or support processing; people with kidney disease must avoid excessive potassium intake. Excess potassium can disturb heart rhythm in sensitive individuals.

name: calcium sulfate
description_en: A mineral ingredient also known as food-grade gypsum, used for firming, flour treatment, and tofu production. Health: Very high intake can cause digestive discomfort or unnecessarily increase calcium exposure; normal food use is generally low risk.

name: aluminum sulfate
description_en: E520 is an aluminum-containing processing salt used in limited applications that contributes to total dietary aluminum exposure. Aluminum can accumulate, so repeated exposure may exceed tolerable weekly levels, especially in those with reduced kidney function.

name: sodium aluminum sulfate
description_en: E521 is an aluminum- and sodium-containing industrial salt used in baking powders and processing applications. Frequent consumption raises concerns due to cumulative aluminum and sodium exposure.
aliases: sulfate d aluminium et de sodium

name: potassium aluminum sulfate
description_en: Potassium alum (E522) is a firming or processing agent that adds aluminum to the diet. Health concerns focus on cumulative aluminum exposure, not immediate effects.
aliases: sulfate d aluminium et de potassium

name: ammonium aluminum sulfate
description_en: E523 is an aluminum-containing industrial salt used for firming or processing in limited foods. Repeated intake contributes to total aluminum exposure, which can accumulate in the body.
aliases: sulfate d aluminium et d ammonium

name: ammonium hydroxide
description_en: An ammonia solution used in controlled processing and pH adjustment. Most ammonia is removed, reacted, or present at very low residual levels. Health: High residual concentrations would irritate the eyes, airways, and digestive tract and produce a strong odor.

name: magnesium hydroxide
description_en: E528 is a refined magnesium compound used to regulate acidity and acts as a laxative at medicinal doses. Too much can cause diarrhea, cramping, and magnesium accumulation in people with kidney impairment.

name: calcium oxide
description_en: Also called quicklime, it is a highly reactive industrial material used in controlled processing. It reacts to form less aggressive calcium compounds. Health: The raw powder is corrosive and can burn tissue. Finished food must not contain unsafe unreacted residues.

name: magnesium oxide
description_en: E530 is a refined magnesium compound used to prevent clumping or regulate acidity. Large doses may cause diarrhea or magnesium accumulation, particularly in people with impaired kidney function.

name: calcium ferrocyanide
description_en: A stable mineral complex used to keep salt and powders free-flowing. Health: No major safety concern is established at authorized use levels. The principal controls are dose and chemical purity.

name: calcium silicate
description_en: A mineral anti-caking agent used in dry powders. Modern long-term toxicology data have been insufficient for a fully updated safety conclusion. Health: The concern is incomplete evidence on repeated exposure, not a proven disease effect at ordinary food levels.

name: magnesium silicate
description_en: A processed mineral used to keep powders dry and free-flowing. The available modern data are limited for a complete long-term assessment. Health: Use should remain controlled because chronic exposure has not been characterized as thoroughly as for better-studied additives.

name: magnesium trisilicate
description_en: A mineral anti-caking compound used in powdered foods. Its long-term safety database is incomplete. Health: The concern is uncertainty from limited chronic and reproductive data, rather than confirmed toxicity from normal food use.

name: gluconic acid
description_en: An organic acid produced from glucose and used to regulate acidity or bind minerals. Health: It has low toxicity, although concentrated or high amounts may irritate the digestive system.

name: sodium gluconate
description_en: E576 is a refined sodium salt used to bind metals, stabilize products, and control acidity. Its main nutritional concern is added sodium rather than specific toxicity.

name: potassium gluconate
description_en: E577 is a potassium salt used for mineral fortification and product stability. Excess potassium can be dangerous for people with kidney disease or medicines that impair potassium removal.

name: calcium gluconate
description_en: E578 is a calcium salt used for firming, fortification, and stabilization. Very high calcium intake can cause constipation and may be unsuitable for people with certain kidney or calcium-balance disorders.

name: ferrous gluconate
description_en: An iron salt used to darken olives and provide iron. It can significantly increase iron exposure in concentrated products. Health: Excess iron can cause nausea, constipation, abdominal pain, and oxidative injury. It is especially dangerous in large accidental doses to children.

name: ferrous lactate
description_en: An iron salt used mainly to stabilize the dark color of olives and other foods. Health: Too much iron may cause digestive symptoms and is unsuitable for people with iron-overload disorders.

name: 4-hexylresorcinol
description_en: A synthetic anti-browning agent used mainly on crustaceans to slow discoloration. Current use is narrow and residue-controlled. Health: No major concern is established at authorized residues. Broader or higher exposure would require additional safety evidence.

name: argon
description_en: An inert gas used to displace oxygen and slow oxidation in packaged food and beverages. Health: It does not react significantly with food and is not considered a safety concern in authorized packaging use.

name: helium
description_en: An inert gas used in specialized packaging or processing. It leaves no meaningful chemical residue in food. Health: Food use is not considered a safety concern. Inhalation of pressurized helium is a separate non-food hazard.

name: oxygen
description_en: A natural gas used in controlled-atmosphere packaging and processing. Health: It is not toxic at food-packaging exposure. It can accelerate oxidation, rancidity, and vitamin loss in some foods.

name: hydrogen
description_en: A gas used in limited food-processing applications. It is highly flammable during industrial handling but does not remain as a toxic food residue. Health: The main hazard is fire or explosion during manufacturing, not consumption of properly processed food.

name: polyvinylpolypyrrolidone (pvpp)
description_en: A synthetic, insoluble polymer used to clarify beverages or stabilize supplements. It is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract. Health: Safety depends on strict limits for residual monomers and manufacturing impurities.

name: polyvinyl alcohol (pva)
description_en: A synthetic polymer used in edible films, coatings, and supplement capsules. It is only partly absorbed and is used for a technological purpose. Health: The principal concern is product purity and residual manufacturing chemicals rather than a proven toxic effect at permitted levels.

name: pullulan
description_en: A fermentation-produced carbohydrate polymer used to make edible films, capsules, and coatings. Health: Several grams at once may cause abdominal fullness, gas, bloating, or cramps in some people.

name: basic methacrylate copolymer
description_en: A synthetic polymer used mainly to coat food supplements and control how tablets dissolve. Health: It is poorly absorbed. Safety relies on low residual monomers, controlled purity, and restricted use.

name: oxidized starch
description_en: Starch chemically oxidised (E1404) to improve thickening, clarity and processing performance. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of the whole modified-starch family found no safety concern and no genotoxic concern. Its role is purely technological: a refined carbohydrate that signals an industrially engineered texture.

name: phosphated distarch phosphate
description_en: A cross-linked and phosphorylated starch (E1413) designed to resist heat, acid and mechanical processing. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the additive brings no nutrition and marks a heavily formulated product.

name: amidon hydroxypropyl
description_en: A chemically modified starch (E1440) that stays stable through freezing, heating and storage. EFSA's 2017 opinion raised no safety or genotoxicity concern, but it is a refined carbohydrate whose only purpose is texture in industrial recipes.

name: acetylated oxidized starch
description_en: A starch both oxidised and acetylated (E1451) to improve stability, clarity and texture. EFSA found no safety concern for the modified-starch family, but the double chemical treatment leaves a refined carbohydrate used purely as a structural ingredient.

name: triethyl citrate
description_en: E1505 is a manufactured citrate ester used as a carrier, solvent, or plasticizer for flavors and coatings. No major specific harm is established at authorized levels; total exposure should remain within the acceptable daily intake.

name: glyceryl diacetate (diacetin)
description_en: E1517 is a manufactured glycerol ester used to carry flavors, retain moisture, and improve processing. It is broken down into glycerol and acetic acid, and no major risk is established at permitted use.

name: benzyl alcohol
description_en: E1519 is an aromatic alcohol used mainly as a solvent or carrier in flavorings. Large systemic doses can depress the nervous system and disturb metabolism; newborns are particularly vulnerable to high medicinal exposure, although food amounts are far lower.

name: propylene glycol
description_en: A synthetic solvent and moisture-retaining agent used in flavors, colors, enzymes, and processed foods. It is not the same substance as toxic ethylene glycol. Health: Very high exposure can cause hyperosmolality, lactic acidosis, nervous-system depression, and kidney stress, especially in infants or people with impaired liver or kidney function.

name: amidon octenylsuccinate de sodium
description_en: Starch modified with octenyl succinic anhydride (E1450) to act as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent in drinks, dressings and powdered flavourings. EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches found no safety concern and no need for a numerical ADI, but it remains a refined carbohydrate with no nutrients and a marker of industrial formulation.

name: propyl paraben
description_en: A paraben preservative removed from the EU list of authorised food additives in 2006, after EFSA judged that the presumed safe intake was no longer valid because of effects on sex hormones and male reproductive organs in young rats. No food ADI has been accepted since. It is still permitted in US food, and was banned from foods in California in 2023.

name: extrait riche en tocopherols
description_en: A natural vitamin E mixture extracted from vegetable oils (E306), used to stop fats going rancid. EFSA's 2015 re-evaluation of the tocopherol family found no safety concern at dietary exposures. It is one of the most benign antioxidants available, and a better sign on a label than synthetic BHA or BHT.

name: lait cru
description_en: Milk that has not been pasteurised. It keeps enzymes and flavour that heat destroys, but it can carry listeria, salmonella and E. coli, which is why health agencies advise against it for pregnant women, young children, older adults and anyone immunocompromised. Its sale for direct consumption is prohibited in Canada.

name: farine de ble blanche
description_en: Wheat flour with the bran and germ milled out. It keeps the starch and part of the protein but loses most of the fibre, magnesium and B vitamins of the grain, and raises blood sugar faster. Wholemeal flour is the same ingredient with its nutrition intact.

name: riz blanc
description_en: Rice polished to remove the bran and germ. It is easy to digest and keeps well, but the milling takes away most of the fibre, magnesium and B vitamins and leaves a starch with a high glycemic response. Basmati has a lower glycemic index than short-grain white rice.

name: sauce soja
description_en: Traditionally brewed soy sauce is fermented for months and carries the depth that comes with it. Two things are worth checking on the label: it is extremely salty, so a few tablespoons cover a large share of the daily sodium limit; and cheaper versions are made by acid hydrolysis rather than brewing, a process that can generate 3-MCPD, which the EU caps by law.

name: miso
description_en: Soybeans fermented with koji over months, eaten as a paste. Unpasteurised miso, natto and tempeh carry live cultures and enzymes that support digestion, along with complete plant protein. Miso is salty enough to count as a seasoning rather than an ingredient.

name: sauce hoisin
description_en: A sweet, thick condiment built mainly on sugar and fermented soybean paste, usually alongside modified starch, caramel colour and flavour enhancers. Oyster sauce is formulated the same way. They are industrial sauces rather than traditional ferments - heavy in both sugar and sodium.

name: sauce poisson
description_en: Anchovies salted and fermented for months, the backbone of South-East Asian cooking. It is a genuine traditional ferment rich in free amino acids, and it is also one of the saltiest condiments in any kitchen - a teaspoon carries as much sodium as a portion of crisps.

name: klamath
description_en: A wild-harvested cyanobacterium (Aphanizomenon flos-aquae) sold as a supplement. Because it is gathered from an open lake rather than cultivated, batches can be contaminated with microcystins, liver toxins produced by other cyanobacteria growing alongside it. Health agencies have repeatedly flagged this, and it is not recommended for children or during pregnancy.

name: taro
description_en: Starchy tropical roots that must always be cooked. Raw taro and raw yam contain calcium oxalate crystals and other compounds that irritate the mouth and digestive tract; cooking destroys them. Once cooked they are a good source of complex carbohydrate, potassium and fibre.

name: pousses de bambou
description_en: Bamboo shoots are low in calories and a good source of fibre and potassium, but fresh shoots contain cyanogenic glycosides and must be boiled before eating - canned shoots are already processed and safe. Bean sprouts and lotus root, often sold alongside them, raise no such issue.

name: fletan
description_en: A large flatfish with firm white flesh and a good omega-3 content. Being a big predator it accumulates more methylmercury than small white fish, which puts it on the FDA and EPA Good Choices list: one serving a week rather than the two to three allowed for lean white fish. Sturgeon falls in the same group.

name: espadon
description_en: Long-lived top predators that concentrate the most methylmercury of any commercial fish. The FDA and EPA place swordfish, shark, marlin, king mackerel, bigeye tuna, orange roughy and Gulf tilefish on the Choices to Avoid list: pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children should not eat them at all, and other adults only rarely.

name: tzatziki
description_en: Dips built on vegetables, yoghurt or nuts: tzatziki from cucumber and yoghurt, guacamole from avocado, baba ganoush from grilled aubergine, romesco and salsa verde from peppers, nuts and herbs. Made at home they are whole ingredients blended together, with nothing added.

name: aioli
description_en: An emulsion of oil, egg yolk and garlic - essentially a garlic mayonnaise. Made with olive oil it is a good fat, but it is almost entirely fat: a couple of tablespoons carry more calories than the dish they accompany.

name: wasabi
description_en: Wasabi and horseradish are pungent roots from the brassica family, grated fresh and used in tiny amounts. Worth knowing that most wasabi sold in tubes and served in restaurants outside Japan is horseradish coloured green, with mustard and dye rather than real wasabi rhizome - the ingredient list will say.

name: pain plat
description_en: Flatbreads such as pita, naan, chapati, roti, lavash and tortilla. Made with wholemeal flour they are a good bread; made with refined white flour, which is the usual case, they behave like white bread, and industrial versions add oils, sugar and preservatives on top.

name: kombucha
description_en: Sweetened tea fermented by a culture of bacteria and yeast. The fermentation consumes part of the sugar and produces organic acids and live cultures, but commercial bottles are usually sweetened again afterwards and can carry as much sugar as a soft drink. The nutrition label settles it, not the health framing.

name: sirop de dattes
description_en: Dates cooked down into a syrup. It keeps some of the potassium and polyphenols of the fruit, but the fibre is largely gone and what remains is concentrated fruit sugar, counted as a free sugar in dietary guidelines.

name: melon
description_en: Melons and watermelon are more than 90% water, which makes them low in calories while supplying potassium, vitamin C and, in the orange and red varieties, beta-carotene and lycopene. Their sugar is diluted enough that a generous portion stays modest.

name: kiwi
description_en: One of the richest fruits in vitamin C, alongside fibre, potassium and actinidin, an enzyme that helps break down protein and eases digestion.

name: coing
description_en: Quince, mirabelle, greengage and morello cherry are stone or pome fruits eaten cooked or fresh, supplying fibre, potassium and polyphenols. Quince is always cooked, being too astringent raw.

name: tamarin
description_en: Tamarind pulp is tangy and high in fibre, magnesium and polyphenols, used as a souring agent across South Asian and Latin American cooking. It is also naturally sugar-dense, so the concentrated pastes and blocks count as a sweet-sour ingredient rather than a fruit portion.

name: physalis
description_en: Small tart fruits eaten fresh - physalis, tamarillo and feijoa. They are low in sugar and supply vitamin C, fibre and carotenoids.
